note: Verse of the Day SOAP cards. Key = VOTD reference. o=Observation, a=Application, p=Prayer/Declaration.

PSA 139:13-16.o: You are NOT an accident. You are intentionally planned and designed by your Heavenly Father. You have a call and purpose.
PSA 139:13-16.a: When you feel unseen or unloved, say it out loud: "God planned me on purpose." Thank Him today for one thing He designed in you.
PSA 139:13-16.p: I am loved and hand-formed by God. I am valuable and have been made for a great purpose.

ROM 10:9.o: Choosing to follow Jesus moves you from the kingdom of Satan to the kingdom of light!
ROM 10:9.a: If you haven't yet, confess Jesus as Lord out loud today. If you have, tell one person about your decision to follow Him.
ROM 10:9.p: I declare that Jesus is my Lord; I will live for Him.

PSA 37:23-24.o: There’s a priority principle in these verses. When you make God’s ways a priority, He makes your ways secure. Often we want security or guarantees from God before we start applying His Word. But, it’s actually the application of His Word that stabilizes our lives.
PSA 37:23-24.a: Put God's ways first in one area of your life this week, then watch Him steady your steps. Don't wait for guarantees before you obey.
PSA 37:23-24.p: I will make God’s plans my priority, and He will establish my steps.

MRK 6:4-5.o: God is all-powerful, yet this passage shows a season where His power was limited. This reveals that we are often the biggest limiter in God’s ability to work in and through our lives. Jesus says he did minimal healing work in this city due to the lack of honor.
MRK 6:4-5.a: Honor Jesus today by putting Him first in a specific decision. Ask Him where your doubt or dishonor may be limiting what He can do.
MRK 6:4-5.p: Jesus, I honor you and put you first in my life! You are my Savior and King! My life is yours!

1TI 6:17.o: We should work hard and create wealth like the Bible tells us we’ve been given the power to do. But where is your hope and trust? Is it in the economy? Is it in the latest stock market strength? Is it in the housing market? Or is your hope in Jesus?
1TI 6:17.a: Check where your hope really sits: your income, the markets, or Jesus. Place one financial worry in His hands today and be generous with something.
1TI 6:17.p: I will not put my hope in money. I will trust in God.

1TH 1:3.o: Cause and effect are happening in this verse. Faith produces work, love prompts serving, and hope in Jesus gives strength to endure. It was the same for Jesus. He was able to endure the cross because he knew it was the only way to save people like us and that brought him joy (Hebrews 12:2).
1TH 1:3.a: Name the work your faith and love are asking of you right now. Take one small step on it today, and let hope in Jesus carry you through.
1TH 1:3.p: I will walk in the faith, hope, and love of God!

ROM 12:12.o: Worship while you wait! While you’re waiting for that thing you’re hoping for, keep praising. All through Scripture God highlights worship and thankfulness. When Jesus heals ten lepers and only one comes back to say thank you, Jesus asks where the rest of them are (Luke 17:17).
ROM 12:12.a: Worship while you wait. Thank God out loud for something He hasn't yet done, and bring Him a thank-you offering today.
ROM 12:12.p: I will be thankful and worship while I wait for the promises of God to be fulfilled.

PSA 71:5.o: You may not have known God since your youth, but you can be confident that no matter when you connected with God, He will be faithful through every age—just like a parent to a child.
PSA 71:5.a: Remember a time God felt close, even in a hard season. Thank Him that He has been faithful to you at every age, and trust Him with what's ahead.
PSA 71:5.p: God is personally walking with me in all seasons of life! I will put my hope in His faithfulness!

ISA 57:18-19.o: God is so gracious to bring peace and healing to all who come to Him! Even when our actions and attitudes don’t deserve His love. It’s clear here that God is initiating healing, guidance, and restoration out of his grace as a means of drawing his people close.
ISA 57:18-19.a: Come to God as you are today, not as you think you should be. Ask Him for the peace and healing He has already promised.
ISA 57:18-19.p: You, Lord, are the giver of peace and healing! I will call on you and watch your work deliverance!

JER 33:6-7.o: Our Father is a restorer of what was lost. He restores sanity, freedom, possessions, and more. While we will face difficult seasons in life, God desires that you live in peace and security. He wants to defend and guard you from the attacks of the enemy and injustice by evil people.
JER 33:6-7.a: Ask the Lord to restore what has been lost in your life: peace, health, relationships, freedom. Pray for it by name, and expect Him to answer.
JER 33:6-7.p: Lord, bring freedom, healing, and restoration of all areas and things the enemy has stolen.

GAL 5:22-23.o: Fruit is the product of a seed. In the same way, when we open up our lives and hearts to the Spirit of God, He’ll plant seeds of love, joy, peace, and all those qualities mentioned in Galatians 5:22-23. As we keep cultivating those seeds, we’ll find they begin to produce that same life in us.
GAL 5:22-23.a: Pick one fruit of the Spirit you need most today and ask Him to grow it. Plant good seeds by what you read, watch, and say.
GAL 5:22-23.p: I will walk in step with the Holy Spirit. As I follow the Holy Spirit, I will produce the fruit of the Spirit.

1CO 15:19.o: Your hope is not temporary. Your hope in Jesus is not just a feel-good fairy tale that numbs the pain of earth. Your hope is eternal. The Apostle Paul says if we’re just doing religion for this life, people should feel sorry for us. But our hope is for life and the life to come.
1CO 15:19.a: Remember that your hope reaches beyond this life. When today's troubles press in, fix your eyes on the eternal hope you have in Jesus.
1CO 15:19.p: My hope is Jesus so my hope is eternal!

MAT 9:23-25.o: Because Jesus knew that death wasn’t final, He could see beyond the natural limitations of death. When we’re facing difficult diagnoses or tragedies, it’s key that we keep our words in alignment with God’s Word! Are you speaking words of life or death over your circumstances?
MAT 9:23-25.a: Speak words of life over your situation today. Pick one circumstance and say what God's Word says about it, not what fear says.
MAT 9:23-25.p: Lord, give us eyes to see how you see! We will stand in faith and pray in alignment with your Word!

2TI 2:22.o: Evil desires and temptations are going to come. We often try to fight temptation when The Bible more often calls us to run from it or avoid it. Most of the sins we fall into can be avoided by staying away. King Solomon warned us to stay away from the home of the temptress.
2TI 2:22.a: Identify one situation, place, or screen that pulls you toward temptation, and walk away from it. Replace it with something that builds faith, love, and peace.
2TI 2:22.p: I will run from temptation and give my life to pursue the purposes of God.

1PE 3:14-16.o: We’ll wrap up these fifty-two verses on hope by calling all of us to continue to spread love and hope to the world around us. You have encountered the hope that is in Jesus. Now, are you ready to give a reason for that hope? Why are you hopeful? Why are you full of joy?
1PE 3:14-16.a: Be ready with your answer. Write down in a sentence or two why you have hope, then share it with someone this week.
1PE 3:14-16.p: I will be ready to give the reason for this great hope!

GAL 2:20.o: Before Jesus, we were trapped by sin and not just trapped but truly spiritually dead. Then Jesus came along and breathed life in us. He brought us back to life! And now, we’re no longer living for just ourselves but we’re living for and in Christ.
GAL 2:20.a: Surrender one plan to Jesus today and say, "Not my will, but Yours." Ask Him what He wants you to do next, then do it.
GAL 2:20.p: I will live each day to honor Jesus and build His Kingdom. Not my will, but God’s will be done!

GAL 1:10.o: Who are you trying to please? One of the greatest dangers in life is trying to attain the approval of others. We should live in a way that fulfills our calling, and if we’re in school or on the job, we honor God by excelling at what we’ve been given.
GAL 1:10.a: Before one decision today, ask, "Am I doing this to please God or to impress people?" Choose to please God, and do your work with excellence.
GAL 1:10.p: I honor God and man, but I will live to please God with all that I think, say, and do.

1PE 1:13.o: Did you know you have a hope bank? And you have a choice where to set and invest that hope. Set your hope on God’s grace. His grace is so powerful because His grace isn’t dependent on my performance or what I say; it’s based on Him. The stock market rises and falls based on issues of the day.
1PE 1:13.a: Set your hope on God's grace today, especially if you failed lately. Receive His forgiveness and start again, because His grace doesn't depend on your performance.
1PE 1:13.p: God’s grace allows me to continue in hope even when I fail.

LUK 6:38.o: Life is way more about what you’re giving than what you’re getting. The world’s system can often be about how much you’re growing and increasing for yourself, but as a follower of Jesus, we know that the secret is in giving. It’s a powerful promise that when you give it’s going to come back.
LUK 6:38.a: Give something away today: a meal, a gift, a kind act, your time. Trust that God sees it and will take care of you.
LUK 6:38.p: As I give I will also receive. God is faithful to generously bless those who live generously.

EPH 6:13.o: When a soldier goes into a battle, they make sure to put on their armor and choose their weapons. In the same way, we are in a spiritual battle and must armor up. Satan wants to stop God’s plans and cause damage to God’s people, but we have been given powerful weapons and armor.
EPH 6:13.a: Put on your armor today. Pick one verse to speak when temptation comes, because the Word is your sword.
EPH 6:13.p: Jesus has given me authority over the devil. God gave us armor to defend against the devil’s attacks and gave us weapons to defeat him.

GEN 1:1-3.o: We begin our study of miracles, reminding ourselves that the one we look to is not a human with limitations or a false idol that people worship, but we’re looking to the one who created the heavens and earth! God sits above it all and holds everything together by His Word!
GEN 1:1-3.a: Bring one impossible situation to the Creator today. Remind yourself that nothing is too hard for the God who made everything.
GEN 1:1-3.p: Nothing is too difficult for God! He is the Creator and sustainer of all life! Miracles are released in His Name!

1CO 6:18.o: This verse is truly a life hack. Often when trying to live for Christ we can accidentally focus too much on not sinning rather than on doing what’s right. The Apostle Paul tells us to flee from sin.
1CO 6:18.a: Don't just avoid the wrong thing. Run toward what's right. Decide today which temptation you'll flee from and what you'll pursue instead.
1CO 6:18.p: I will run after God and live a righteous life.

ROM 15:13.o: A life of hope in God produces joy and peace. The Holy Spirit causes us to overflow with hope. In modern self-help teaching, it’s purely up to you to make all of the happiness and hope happen.
ROM 15:13.a: Ask the Holy Spirit to fill you with joy and peace as you trust Him. Don't try to manufacture hope. Receive it from the God of hope.
ROM 15:13.p: He is the God of hope. I will walk in joy and peace as I trust Him!

LUK 16:10.o: One of the vital principles of promotion in life is to be faithful with what you have now, even if it’s not much. God is good and doesn’t want to bless you beyond what you are ready for, so He’ll watch how you handle “little” before you’re promoted to “much.”
LUK 16:10.a: Be faithful with one small thing today, whether it's your time, money, or responsibility at work. Handle it as though God is watching, because He is.
LUK 16:10.p: I will be faithful and multiply what I am given.

LUK 2:52.o: As Jesus was fully God and fully human, He still had to go through the growing-up phases of life through childhood and teenage years. Luke 2:52 gives us a snapshot of the four areas that He developed in. Wisdom, stature, favor with God and with Man.
LUK 2:52.a: Rate your growth in wisdom, body, relationships, and spiritual life. Set one small goal in the area that needs the most attention.
LUK 2:52.p: I will continue to grow and strengthen my mind, body, soul, and spirit!

PSA 119:81.o: Sometimes we’re afraid to be honest about where we’re at in life. But King David shows us how to be vulnerable with the heaviness or pain that we’re walking through. He then directs himself back to hope in God.
PSA 119:81.a: Be honest with God about where you are today. Then, like David, turn your heart back toward hope. Choose two verses to repeat when you feel tired.
PSA 119:81.p: Even when I feel tired, God will remain faithful.

PSA 62:5.o: From time to time you may feel like you don’t even have the ability to hope anymore. But that’s how good God is—not only is He the one that we want to put our hope in, but He is also the giver of hope. When you’re up against a wall and feeling overwhelmed, lean into and spend time with Jesus.
PSA 62:5.a: Take time to rest in God today. Quiet your phone, pray, and read the Bible for a few minutes. Remember that He is the source of your hope.
PSA 62:5.p: God is where my soul truly finds rest and refreshing. My hope comes from God.

MRK 5:25-29.o: This engagement that a suffering woman has with Jesus tells us so much. First, we all deal with this reality: the fatigue of trying and getting nowhere in your health or any area of your life. It’s easy to give up, but her persistence teaches us to never give up on our healing!
MRK 5:25-29.a: If you're tired of trying, don't quit. Reach out to Jesus again today and ask for healing, like the woman who pressed through the crowd.
MRK 5:25-29.p: One touch from Jesus can heal and restore all things!

JAS 5:13-14.o: These verses are packed with instruction on worship, prayer, healing, and the power of the church community. We’ll focus on the truth that God wants you to come to Him when you’re in need. You don’t have to be afraid of coming close to God; you’re not bothering Him with your requests.
JAS 5:13-14.a: You aren't bothering God. Bring Him one specific request today, and thank Him for one thing He's already done.
JAS 5:13-14.p: God, I am thankful for your goodness. When I call on your name, you will answer me.

MAL 3:10-12.o: When praying for financial provision or breakthrough, it’s vital to ask the honor and tithing questions. Are you honoring God with the first 10% of all that you make? If you’re a tither, you can claim the promises and pray in alignment with the open heaven over your lives.
MAL 3:10-12.a: Pray with honor: give God your first and best from your income. Then ask for provision, standing on His promise.
MAL 3:10-12.p: I will honor the Lord in faithfully bringing my tithes! I will stand on his promise of blessing and protection!

PSA 23:1-4.o: These are great verses to read often. It speaks of God’s desire to bring us peace and to lead us into good things. He desires that you lack nothing! These verses give us a promise, that no matter what dark and painful season we may be facing, God will never leave us.
PSA 23:1-4.a: Read Psalm 23 slowly today. Remember a hard time when God was still with you, and let that memory quiet your fear.
PSA 23:1-4.p: I will follow the leading of the Good Shepherd. I will not live in fear because He is with me!

1CH 16:11-12.o: It’s so easy to forget the good and hold onto the negative things that have happened to us. But God’s Word constantly reminds us to call to memory the good. Remember the miracles, the moments where God came through, the wisdom and creativity that He brought, the justice that was done.
1CH 16:11-12.a: Write down three ways God has come through for you. Thank Him for each of them out loud.
1CH 16:11-12.p: I will look to God and remember His goodness! I will praise Him for all His wisdom and miracles.

PSA 103:2-5.o: These few verses will inject faith and hope into your soul no matter what you’re facing! These are verses that you can hold onto and use to pray through any giants you’re facing. The key here is to begin by keeping a heart of thankfulness.
PSA 103:2-5.a: Pray Psalm 103 as your own prayer today. Start by thanking Him, then bring the giants you face.
PSA 103:2-5.p: You are my savior, healing, and redeemer! You love to do good to your children! I am satisfied in you!

MAT 6:19-21.o: Having an eternal perspective is key to a fulfilled life on earth. Why? Because the eternal provides the context and purpose for this life. Many live aimlessly and, therefore, make no impact. But, when you live and do everything from a biblical perspective, it brings life into focus.
MAT 6:19-21.a: Invest in something eternal today. Give, serve, or encourage someone, and let heaven shape how you spend your time and money.
MAT 6:19-21.p: I will store up treasures in heaven by investing my time and resources into the things on earth that are eternal.

JHN 16:33.o: Becoming a Christian won’t necessarily make your life easier; there will always be trouble in our world because of sin. Yes, there is a lot of self-inflicted pain that we begin to avoid due to living according to the Bible.
JHN 16:33.a: Bring today's trouble to Jesus and take His peace. Remind yourself that He has already overcome whatever you're facing.
JHN 16:33.p: No matter what trouble comes my way, I will have peace and walk out the victory Jesus has already won.

JHN 3:16-17.o: This is one of the most well-known verses in the world because it gives us a simple overview of how valuable we are to God and what Jesus did to provide salvation for us. Jesus left heaven and came to earth as a man to pay the price for all of humanity’s sins.
JHN 3:16-17.a: Take a minute to receive God's love: He gave His Son for you. Then share this good news with one person today.
JHN 3:16-17.p: I am loved and valuable. I have put my hope and faith in Jesus!

JHN 8:32.o: God’s Word is Truth. But the culture around you is hurting, broken, and in bondage, because it doesn’t know or receive that truth. Only the truths in the Bible can answer life’s toughest questions and give hope and purpose.
JHN 8:32.a: Read one passage today and ask what truth it speaks into your struggle. Pray for a friend who needs freedom that only God's truth can bring.
JHN 8:32.p: I will submit to God’s truth and walk in freedom.

MAT 7:24-27.o: What foundation are you building your life on? Jesus calls us to build on the only sure and solid foundation, which is His Word. Following the ideas and thoughts from this world is like building your house on a shaky and uncertain foundation.
MAT 7:24-27.a: Choose one area that feels shaky and rebuild it on God's Word. Memorize one verse and put it into action this week.
MAT 7:24-27.p: My life will be built on the foundation of God’s Word.

PRO 4:20-22.o: God’s Word brings life and light everywhere it’s sent! The Bible says that he sustains everything by the power of His Word! To keep healthy and strong in all areas of the natural and supernatural, we will need a constant intake of God’s Word.
PRO 4:20-22.a: Take in God's Word every day, not just on Sundays. Pick one verse to speak over your health, your mind, and your home.
PRO 4:20-22.p: God’s Word is life and healing to my body and soul! I will engage and speak His Word daily!

2CO 4:16-18.o: Trouble produces either strength or bitterness in our lives, but it will always produce something. The key is for us as believers to keep the right perspective and right focus. When you approach difficulty as a chance to grow and allow God to teach you something, you’ll see incredible dividends.
2CO 4:16-18.a: Ask God, "What are You teaching me through this?" Choose a better perspective today and refuse to let difficulty make you bitter.
2CO 4:16-18.p: I trust that God is working in the seen and unseen moments to bring about His purpose in my life!

MRK 10:42-45.o: As men, we’re called to lead in our homes and in our world. Jesus set the example and called us to lead by serving. This simple but powerful approach will take your impact to a new level with your family, coworkers, staff, and the world around you. Servant leadership changes how you engage people.
MRK 10:42-45.a: Lead by serving today. Ask your family, coworkers, or team, "What do you need from me?" and then do it.
MRK 10:42-45.p: I will not hold back from a leadership role in my family, work, and church. I will help others succeed.

1TI 6:10-11.o: Money is a massive part of our lives because it’s how we live, build the economy, and engage with others. Money can be incredibly helpful, and money can corrupt and destroy. From these verses, we see the issue isn’t money but the love of it.
1TI 6:10-11.a: Make sure money is your tool and not your master. Give generously today to someone in need, without expecting anything back.
1TI 6:10-11.p: I will be generous with all God has blessed me with.

MAT 5:14-16.o: Your relationship with God is personal but it’s not meant to stay private or hidden. Jesus saved you and put His light inside your life and now He wants to set you up as a light that guides people back home. You don’t have to be perfect to shine your light.
MAT 5:14-16.a: Let your light shine today. Tell someone you follow Jesus, or invite a friend to church. You don't have to be perfect to shine.
MAT 5:14-16.p: I will shine bright and point people to Jesus! I will not hide the good news. I will live out my faith in all areas!

MAT 28:18-20.o: As followers of Jesus, we’re not just here taking up space; we’re on a mission. The mandate to increase and take dominion began in the Garden of Eden with Adam and Eve, but Jesus calls us back to that mission when He says to make and increase disciples on the earth.
MAT 28:18-20.a: Make disciples where you already are. Choose one person, starting at home, and show them what it looks like to follow Jesus.
MAT 28:18-20.p: I will own the great commission from Jesus to make disciples of all nations, starting with my family.

LUK 13:11-13.o: Notice first that it was a spirit that had been crippling her, not just a birth defect. The demonic hold on people's minds and bodies can be very real and challenging, which is why we must take authority and break off those demonic strongholds.
LUK 13:11-13.a: Ask God for discernment. Pray over anyone you know who feels trapped or crippled, and take authority in Jesus' name.
LUK 13:11-13.p: Lord, give me discernment to see any demonic activity oppressing myself or those in my world. I will bring freedom to people crippled by demonic activity.

EPH 2:8-9.o: Your salvation from sin is not something that happens by being a good person. You may have heard that if your good deeds outweigh your bad deeds, that will get you into heaven. However, the Bible is clear that we’re saved and forgiven because of the grace of God displayed on the cross.
EPH 2:8-9.a: Rest in grace. Thank Jesus that your salvation is a gift, not something earned by being good.
EPH 2:8-9.p: I am loved and forgiven by God. His grace has saved me.

PRO 13:20.o: The friends that you hang out with the most are who you become like. We want to be friendly and kind to everyone but choose your close friends wisely.
PRO 13:20.a: Look at who you spend the most time with. Decide whether they're making you wiser, and be that kind of friend to someone else.
PRO 13:20.p: My friends will impact my life for good or bad. I will choose friends wisely and I will grow to be a wise friend others want to hang out with.

MAT 11:28.o: What an incredible invitation from Jesus! When you face difficulty, pain, tragedy, fatigue, bad news, or anything burdening you, Jesus says to come to Him! You don’t have to carry everything alone; you can bring it all to Jesus. What is your default when you face difficulty?
MAT 11:28.a: Name the biggest burden you're carrying. Say it to Jesus right now and ask for His rest, instead of carrying it alone.
MAT 11:28.p: I will bring my worries and fears to Jesus and find peace and strength.

PSA 146:7-8.o: You’ll notice a theme in these verses, “The Lord,” it’s vital to remember that we are not attempting to work miracles and freedom in our own strength, but it’s The Lord who is healing and holding you up through His Strength and power!
PSA 146:7-8.a: Remember that the Lord is the one who lifts you up. Stop trying to fix it in your own strength and ask Him to do what only He can.
PSA 146:7-8.p: The Lord is the lifter and deliverer of my life! I will trust in his faithfulness!

1PE 5:5-6.o: Submission to God and the authority He placed in your life is the beginning of unlocking your strength. There are few things that the Bible says God opposes, and pride is one of them. Learn to humble yourself before God, and wait for His timing and promotion.
1PE 5:5-6.a: Humble yourself today. Ask a trusted person for input or correction, and wait for God's timing instead of forcing it.
1PE 5:5-6.p: I will walk in humility and grace. I will receive input and correction. I will walk in God’s favor!

PSA 18:13-14.o: Life is filled with circumstances that are beyond our control. How do you respond to pain, disaster, loss, the economy, or a health diagnosis? When things seem too difficult or beyond your control, what do you do? The Bible reminds us that we should look to the one who thunders from heaven.
PSA 18:13-14.a: When something feels out of your control, look up. Admit your limits to God and ask for His power in the situation.
PSA 18:13-14.p: God is all-powerful, and I am submitted to His leading. He will right the wrongs done against me.

GEN 8:22.o: The world God created for us is not by chance or in chaos. God’s specific and intentional design holds the universe and the world in which we live in perfect harmony and peace. This is excellent news on a cosmic scale, but it also has very specific implications for your life.
GEN 8:22.a: Remember that God's plans are specific and on purpose. Where life feels uncertain, trust His timing and thank Him that He is in control.
GEN 8:22.p: God, you are specific and perfect in all that you do! All the principles you’ve established will succeed.

GAL 5:5.o: The Holy Spirit continues to be a theme connected to the topic of hope. Through Him, we are encouraged and given the ability to wait for the hope to be fulfilled. The more we lean into the voice of the Holy Spirit, the more at peace we will be in our day-to-day lives.
GAL 5:5.a: Slow down and listen for the Holy Spirit today. Ask Him to give you patience and peace while you wait for what God has promised.
GAL 5:5.p: The Holy Spirit is perfecting me. I walk in the righteousness that Jesus gave me.

MAT 14:14-21.o: God is more than enough! This miraculous provision is recorded in all Gospels and is performed a couple times by Jesus.
MAT 14:14-21.a: Bring God what you have, even if it feels small. Thank Him, and trust Him to multiply it.
MAT 14:14-21.p: I will put my trust in the supernatural power of God! He can multiply what I have into overflow!

EPH 1:17-19.o: What a great hope we have been called to! Often we forget to reflect on His goodness. Our hope in Jesus is of eternal significance! Because of our sin, we had been condemned to hell and eternal separation from God. We were lost and without hope.
EPH 1:17-19.a: Take a moment to thank God for rescuing you from being lost and without hope. Ask Him to open your eyes to the hope you've been called to.
EPH 1:17-19.p: I will walk in the fullness of all that Jesus paid for on the cross.

JAS 5:16.o: If you need healing, begin with confessing your sin; this will kick the devil out of your life so that healing can flow. Sometimes, people are held in physical sickness because of demonic and spiritual oppression.
JAS 5:16.a: Confess anything weighing on you and receive God's forgiveness. Then ask a trusted friend or pastor to pray for you.
JAS 5:16.p: Lord, I confess my sin and ask that you purify me. My prayers are powerful because I’m your Child!

DEU 8:3.o: God calls us into purpose and dominion. As men, we can get arrogant and start thinking our dominion is all our own doing. So, if you’re facing a season of testing and struggle, it may be God’s grace pulling you out beyond your own ability so you can learn to trust God again.
DEU 8:3.a: Make time for God's Word today. Let it feed you before anything else, and ask the Holy Spirit to highlight one thing.
DEU 8:3.p: I do not live by my strength alone; I am dependent on the Word of God for courage, hope, and life!

JAS 4:8.o: What an incredible invitation to all of us! The Creator of the heavens and the earth has called us to be close to Him. You don’t need to be religious or distant. Instead, come close to God. How do we do this? We get close to God by spending time with Him.
JAS 4:8.a: Draw near to God today with ten quiet minutes of prayer, worship, or Scripture. He promises to come near to you.
JAS 4:8.p: My heavenly Father wants to be close to me. I will chase after His presence.

LUK 4:34-35.o: There is a supernatural realm. The unseen realm isn’t just in the afterlife; it’s right now! The supernatural world is all around us. It is from the unseen that all of the visible has come. So, the demons we can't see were able to see that Jesus was not just a carpenter, but the Son of God.
LUK 4:34-35.a: Remember that the unseen realm is real and Jesus has authority over it. Pray with confidence today, speaking His name over what you see.
LUK 4:34-35.p: The unseen has created the seen! We take authority over the natural and supernatural world in Jesus' name!

MAT 6:9-13.o: If you feel unsure how to pray, you’re in good company. The disciples asked Jesus to teach them how to pray, and these verses were His response.
MAT 6:9-13.a: Pray the Lord's Prayer slowly today. Pause at each line and make it personal.
MAT 6:9-13.p: I will boldly approach my heavenly Father. Lord, your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.

PHP 2:3-4.o: These verses “hurt so good.” They are powerful in their effect on your life, but they require an initial step of self-sacrifice that is often uncomfortable or unnatural. Most of life’s challenges come from not applying this scripture.
PHP 2:3-4.a: Ask yourself where you've been selfish this week, then put someone else's needs first today.
PHP 2:3-4.p: I will focus on serving others’ needs before my own.

MAT 6:10.o: Jesus calls us to pray that the Kingdom of Heaven will invade this earth. This is powerful when it comes to believing for miracles. We know that the Kingdom of Heaven has no sickness and disease, no poverty, and no demonic oppression.
MAT 6:10.a: Pray "Your Kingdom come" over your family, work, and city today. Name one place where you want to see heaven break in.
MAT 6:10.p: Lord, let your Kingdom come in my family, work, city, nation, and everywhere I have influence.

PSA 52:9.o: God is good! This is a truth we know by how God has revealed Himself to us in the Bible and throughout human history. But, it’s also the key thing that the devil is always trying to challenge. With Adam and Eve, the devil tried to say that God was holding out on them.
PSA 52:9.a: Write down three things you're thankful for and three worries to hand over to God. Thank Him that He is good.
PSA 52:9.p: You are a good God! All you say and do can be trusted.

PSA 33:16-18.o: What are you putting your hope in? What are you resting your confidence and trust in? Is it in the modern-day version of the horse, which would be our careers, education, or family ties? On this side of eternity, while we need protection and security, ultimately our salvation comes from God.
PSA 33:16-18.a: Name where your confidence really sits: your job, your skills, your savings. Hand that area back to God and trust His strength over your own.
PSA 33:16-18.p: My trust is not in the strength of my hand but in the power of my God!

2CO 3:12.o: My hope in Jesus gives me courage! Because I know who’s behind me, I’m full of hope. It reminds me of the story of David and Goliath; although he was young and much smaller, David had confidence that he could beat the giant Goliath, because God was on David’s side.
2CO 3:12.a: Walk in boldness today, not arrogance. Remember one past victory God gave you, and let it give you courage to step out.
2CO 3:12.p: I will put my hope in God and walk in boldness!

PRO 10:4.o: While God loves you and wants to bless your life in many ways, that doesn’t mean He will just give you everything you want. His blessing is on the work of our hands. When you are faithful, diligent, effective, and productive, God’s blessing will be on that!
PRO 10:4.a: Work as if it matters to God, because it does. Choose one way to be more diligent or add value at your work today.
PRO 10:4.p: I will honor God by being faithful, diligent, and committed to my work.

EPH 6:10-14.o: There is a spiritual battle between demonic forces and the followers of Jesus here on earth. It’s not hyperbole; it’s a real battle—but the good news is that God didn’t leave us without armor and weapons for this battle. Read all of Ephesians 6:10-18 to know all of the pieces of armor.
EPH 6:10-14.a: Put on God's armor today. Name the spiritual pressure you feel and stand firm against it with prayer and the Word.
EPH 6:10-14.p: I am equipped to fight and defeat the enemy.

LUK 6:19.o: Jesus has more than enough power for all to be healed and restored! It was faith that drew out the power from Jesus, and it’s the same today! Do you need a miracle? Go to Jesus with faith and expectation of healing! Notice also that there was a physical flow of a supernatural force.
LUK 6:19.a: If you need a miracle, come to Jesus with faith today. Reach out to Him, and pray for someone who needs healing.
LUK 6:19.p: Faith draws on the power of God! The Holy Spirit will flow through me to heal as I lay my hands on them!

MAT 22:37-39.o: Jesus makes it very simple and clear as to what are the most important things we should know and do as a believer. First is to love God fully and passionately with all you have. How do we do that? By loving God with our work, with our family, with our dreams, and with everything.
MAT 22:37-39.a: Love God with all you have, and love one person well today. Do one thing for someone else that costs you something.
MAT 22:37-39.p: I will love God with every part of my life, and I will love others selflessly.

HEB 4:12-13.o: As men, we’re often the ones with the tool or weapon in our hands taking care of business, but have we opened up our lives to the sword of God? It’s not just any kind of weapon; it’s both powerful and precise. This weapon is the Word of God.
HEB 4:12-13.a: Let God's Word search your heart today. Read one passage and ask, "What is God saying to me?" Then obey it.
HEB 4:12-13.p: God’s Word is alive and active in my life! I will submit to and boldly speak the Word of God.

JHN 3:16.o: This is one of the most well-known verses in the world because it gives us a simple overview of how valuable we are to God and what Jesus did to provide salvation for us. Jesus left heaven and came to earth as a man to pay the price for all of humanity’s sins.
JHN 3:16.a: Take a minute to receive God's love: He gave His Son for you. Then share this good news with one person today.
JHN 3:16.p: I am loved and valuable. I have put my hope and faith in Jesus!

PSA 33:19-21.o: You can put your hope in God no matter the season you find yourself in. Even in a famine, God is able. If we’re not careful, we’ll say we trust God, and then when we see a news story or the stock market update, we go to fear.
PSA 33:19-21.a: Wait for God with expectation, even in a hard season. Thank Him ahead of time for the deliverance you're hoping to see.
PSA 33:19-21.p: I wait in great expectation for God’s deliverance!

1CO 11:23-25.o: Jesus calls us to take communion consistently. What is that? It’s when you eat bread and drink wine or juice to represent what Jesus did for us on the cross. The church you go to may have the whole church take communion often, and you can also practice this on your own.
1CO 11:23-25.a: Take communion thoughtfully this week, whether at church or at home. Thank Jesus for the cross, and receive His healing and covering.
1CO 11:23-25.p: Jesus, your blood heals and covers my life.

JAS 4:10.o: Don’t worry too much about “getting ahead.” Focus more on humbly serving God and others. When you live submitted to God then you’ll see God elevate and promote you in the right way and the right timing.
JAS 4:10.a: Stop striving to get ahead. Serve someone quietly today and trust God to lift you up at the right time.
JAS 4:10.p: I will trust God’s timing and promotion. God’s Word and timing are perfect.

1TI 4:12.o: It’s easy to assume that you have to wait till you’re an adult before you can set the example. But, this verse and many stories throughout the Bible show us that God often chose young people to take on bold and courageous missions.
1TI 4:12.a: Don't wait to be older to lead. Set an example this week in how you speak, love, and live. God can use you right now.
1TI 4:12.p: My youth doesn’t disqualify me. I can lead the way even while I’m young. God often uses young people to change the world!

JAS 4:7-8.o: There’s too much goodness in these verses! First off, all the promises in these verses begin with the recognition and submission to God and His authority in your life.
JAS 4:7-8.a: Submit one area of your life to God today. Then resist the enemy and draw near to God, and He will draw near to you.
JAS 4:7-8.p: I submit my whole life to you, God! I will come close to you and I will kick the devil out of my life!

MAL 3:8-10.o: Tithing is a practice that God calls us to commit to, which is bringing God the first 10 percent of all we earn. This is about priorities, trust, and God’s economy. God doesn’t need our money; He wants our hearts and our trust.
MAL 3:8-10.a: Honor God with your first 10 percent. If you haven't started, decide today to begin, and trust Him with the rest.
MAL 3:8-10.p: I will trust God in my giving and see His blessing in my life. I am blessed so I can be a blessing!

PRO 16:9.o: Plan your steps and submit them to God. Man was created to increase and rule, but we are not a law unto ourselves. We are empowered to the level that we’re submitted to God. For optimal success in life, we must learn to submit our plans to God.
PRO 16:9.a: Write out your plans and offer them to God. Pray over each one and invite Him to change anything that doesn't match His heart.
PRO 16:9.p: I will pray and plan. I want my plans to echo God’s heart and be sustained by His strength!

MAT 7:7-11.o: These verses remind us of two major factors: first, God wants you to ask and keep asking until the answer comes, and second, God wants to give us good things. How often do we quit and stop short in prayer because we get fatigued with the delays or assume God is uninterested?
MAT 7:7-11.a: Ask God for something specific today, and keep asking. Believe that your Father wants to give you good things.
MAT 7:7-11.p: God is good and loves to give us good things! I will ask according to His will and keep seeking and knocking until the answer comes!

PSA 71:13-15.o: Why is King David, the writer of this psalm, declaring hope? Because he understands the nature of God. While God judges and condemns the wicked, David also knows that God blesses and strengthens the righteous. His hope is in God and His ability and desire to bless and strengthen you.
PSA 71:13-15.a: Choose hope today because of who God is. Thank Him that He is on your side, and say aloud one way He has blessed you.
PSA 71:13-15.p: I will always have hope because God is always with me!

PSA 119:11.o: When you put God’s Word into your heart, it has a way of guarding, insulating, and protecting your life against the enemy. The way that you hide God’s Word in your heart is by reading it often—daily if you can—and deciding what you’re going to apply from what you just read.
PSA 119:11.a: Hide a verse in your heart today. Write it down, memorize it, and say it when temptation or worry shows up.
PSA 119:11.p: Your Word guards, protects, and guides my life.

2KI 4:27-28.o: “Don’t get your hopes up” is a phrase that we often hear in our culture. It’s an attempt to stop our risk of disappointment and pain. But this phrase is a trick of the enemy to rob your life. God calls us to great faith, and the devil is always going to tempt you to play it small and safe.
2KI 4:27-28.a: Don't let anyone talk you out of hope. Name the dream or promise God gave you, and bring it back to Him in prayer.
2KI 4:27-28.p: I will keep my hopes up because my hope is in God!

ACT 2:25-27.o: We often underestimate the toll that life can have on us. Work, family, the economy, school, and the news can all begin to drain our energy. When we put our hope in Jesus, it affects our heart and emotions; it changes how we speak; and it impacts the physical body’s ability to rest.
ACT 2:25-27.a: Build rest into your day. Take ten quiet minutes with Jesus, and let your hope in Him keep you steady when life drains you.
ACT 2:25-27.p: I am unshakable because my hope is in the unshakable God!

ISA 40:28-31.o: The Bible says that the joy of the Lord is our strength (Nehemiah 8:10). Hope is in the same vein as joy. When our hope disappears, we’ll find ourselves tired and losing the strength, both physically and mentally, to take on the adventures and challenges of life.
ISA 40:28-31.a: When you're weary, wait on the Lord. Take a few minutes today to rest in Him and ask Him to renew your strength.
ISA 40:28-31.p: I may get weary, but my strength will be renewed as I put my hope in God!

GAL 6:7.o: At first look, this verse might seem like a negative thing like God is watching and ready to make sure you reap bad things from your bad decisions. And yes, you will reap pain from the negative or sinful seeds that you sow, but this verse is also a promise.
GAL 6:7.a: Decide what you want to see grow in your life, then sow into it. Start with one daily habit of faith this week.
GAL 6:7.p: I will reap what I sow. I will see good things in my life as I apply God’s good word.

DEU 8:5.o: God disciplines us because He loves us. He doesn’t want to see us left where we are but instead wants to challenge and call us out of our dysfunctions. This verse also challenges us to be good fathers who commit to disciplining our children.
DEU 8:5.a: Welcome correction today as a sign of God's love. Ask a leader or mentor, "Where can I grow?" and listen without defending yourself.
DEU 8:5.p: I will be open and receptive to the discipline that God and my leaders bring into my life!

PRO 17:22.o: God wants to restore Joy to people; laughter and peace are hallmarks of Christianity. The Bible says that where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom. With so many facing anxiety and depression, they need to know that God can set them free and restore hope and joy.
PRO 17:22.a: Choose joy on purpose today. Laugh, thank God, and don't believe the lies that say life has to be heavy.
PRO 17:22.p: I will walk in the joy of the Lord! I won’t listen to the enemy's lies. I will walk in freedom and experience life!

EST 4:14.o: If you’re breathing, then you have a purpose! Take Esther’s story to heart: the challenges you see around you are not there just for you to feel sad about or just for you to pray about; maybe God positioned you in your workplace, neighborhood, school, or nation for such a time as this.
EST 4:14.a: Ask God what He has positioned you to do. Pick one need around you that bothers you, and take one step to help.
EST 4:14.p: I am positioned for such a time as this. I won’t be silent. I will engage and transform my world.

HEB 13:8.o: It’s almost hard to wrap our heads around a perfect God who has always been and will continue to be. Since we are constantly changing and growing, we might assume that God is like that. But, his character and Word was, is, and will continue to be perfect. Which means it’s reliable.
HEB 13:8.a: Rest in a God who never changes. Where your circumstances shift, remember that His grace and truth stay the same.
HEB 13:8.p: God is perfect and never changes. His grace and truth are constant and forever. He is faithful even if I’m not.

MAT 8:6-10.o: What a powerful picture of someone who understood how the supernatural realm operates and who has authority. This leader saw Jesus as the King that He is; he saw Him as the one who could command the armies of Heaven and command demons and sickness to leave with just a Word!
MAT 8:6-10.a: Come to Jesus with faith that His word is enough. Bring Him one need today and trust that He only has to say the word.
MAT 8:6-10.p: Jesus, you are The King; all heaven and earth respond at your command! Just Say The Word!

ROM 15:4.o: Take trips back in time to remember the faithfulness of God in your life and the lives of others. The Bible is written to give you hope. When I revisit the stories of God’s power, faithfulness, grace, and provision, it calls me toward hope.
ROM 15:4.a: Remember God's faithfulness. Read one story from the Gospels today and let it build your hope.
ROM 15:4.p: My hope increases when I endure and stay faithful!

LUK 5:5-8.o: In obedience, Peter takes the word of Jesus about His business, and God performs a miracle. Maybe you are like Peter, who assumed that God’s Word and power only applied to spiritual or church things, but God’s Word, wisdom, and power are available for all areas of your life.
LUK 5:5-8.a: Obey God's word even when it doesn't make sense. Take the next step He's asked of you and trust Him with the results.
LUK 5:5-8.p: I will trust God’s direction for my family, work, and ministry! Seek God, and He will provide supernatural provision and strategy.

ISA 53:5.o: Jesus went to the cross and dealt with all areas where the curse affected humanity. The curse of sin was spiritual death and brings decay to God’s intended design. We need to see the work of Jesus on the cross as the purchase of freedom and healing for our present and future.
ISA 53:5.a: Jesus took your sin and sickness on the cross. Thank Him for it today, and ask Him for healing in one area where you need it.
ISA 53:5.p: Jesus paid the debt of my sin and sickness! I am healed because He overcame disease and death!

HEB 4:12.o: As men, we’re often the ones with the tool or weapon in our hands taking care of business, but have we opened up our lives to the sword of God? It’s not just any kind of weapon; it’s both powerful and precise. This weapon is the Word of God.
HEB 4:12.a: Let God's Word search your heart today. Read one passage and ask, "What is God saying to me?" Then obey it.
HEB 4:12.p: God’s Word is alive and active in my life! I will submit to and boldly speak the Word of God.

ROM 12:2.o: Every day you have a choice as to what pattern you’re going to model your life after. Will it be the pattern of the world leading to death or the pattern from God found in the Bible that leads to life? As you follow Jesus and His ways, your life will be transformed little by little.
ROM 12:2.a: Don't copy the world's patterns. Pick one thought pattern to replace with God's truth today, and let His Word renew your mind.
ROM 12:2.p: I will build my life on the pattern of God’s Word. I will know and fulfill God’s will for my life.

GEN 1:1.o: We begin our study of miracles, reminding ourselves that the one we look to is not a human with limitations or a false idol that people worship, but we’re looking to the one who created the heavens and earth! God sits above it all and holds everything together by His Word!
GEN 1:1.a: Bring one impossible situation to the Creator today. Remind yourself that nothing is too hard for the God who made everything.
GEN 1:1.p: Nothing is too difficult for God! He is the Creator and sustainer of all life! Miracles are released in His Name!

LUK 4:38-39.o: I love that Jesus cares about the spectacular miracles like raising kids from the dead and the unseen miracle of healing a fever. This miracle reminds us that no matter what you’re facing, you can go to God and ask Him for it.
LUK 4:38-39.a: Jesus cares about the big things and the small things. Bring Him a request you've been holding back, no matter how small it seems.
LUK 4:38-39.p: You care about all my requests! I will stand and use the authority you’ve given me to rebuke sickness!

LUK 17:17.o: Are you indifferent or thankful for God’s goodness? We may feel that’s an obvious yes, but it requires intentionality not to forget His blessings and move too quickly to familiarity.
LUK 17:17.a: Say thank you to God today, specifically. Write down three of His blessings and tell Him you're grateful.
LUK 17:17.p: Thank you, Lord, for your kindness, goodness, and justice! You’re the healer and restorer of my life!

EPH 3:17-19.o: The Apostle Paul begins by calling us to be planted in Christ and let our roots go down deep! Just like a fruit tree must be planted to produce fruit, we must be planted to stand strong and remain fruitful in all seasons.
EPH 3:17-19.a: Get rooted in love. Ask God to show you how deep His love is, and stay connected to your church family this week.
EPH 3:17-19.p: I am committed and planted in the Church! God’s love is never-ending and never failing!

ACT 5:29.o: While God calls us to love, serve, and prefer others above ourselves, there are times when you have to go against what others are saying, even when they are your authority. The disciples knew that if the word of the government ever contradicted the Word of God, they had to choose God over man.
ACT 5:29.a: Choose to obey God over pressure from people. Decide today where you will stand for what's right, and do it with kindness.
ACT 5:29.p: I will obey God and speak the truth even when it’s inconvenient or even if I am persecuted.

1PE 5:7.o: As men, the weight of the world can feel like it’s resting on our shoulders. While God has designed us to carry the weight of our family, finances, and future, God invites us to partner with Him to bear the load.
1PE 5:7.a: Hand your worries to Jesus today. Name each one in prayer and trust that He cares about every detail.
1PE 5:7.p: God cares about every detail of my life. I will bring my worries to Jesus daily in prayer!

PSA 119:147.o: Is your daily routine intentional? King David gives us a window into how he keeps a life full of hope. Instead of waking up aimlessly or waking up and focusing on the negative, he wakes up and cries out to God right away!
PSA 119:147.a: Start your day with God before the world reaches you. Set aside five minutes tomorrow morning to pray and put your hope in Him.
PSA 119:147.p: I will daily call out to the Lord and put my hope in Him!

ECC 9:4.o: If you’re still breathing, you have reason to hope. We love the strength of lions and the majesty that they carry. We can often look at our own lives and feel a lack of hope or strength because we’re not the lion or because we see ourselves more like the dog in comparison.
ECC 9:4.a: While you have breath, you have hope. Stop comparing yourself to others and take one step toward the purpose God gave you.
ECC 9:4.p: I will honor God with every breath that I have. As long as I am living, I have purpose and potential!

PRO 1:7.o: This is another one of those absolute foundations! You might be wondering why we should be afraid of God? God is so awesome and powerful that having a little fear and trembling isn’t a bad thing, but this verse is more about putting God in His proper place in your life.
PRO 1:7.a: Put God first in how you think and decide. Before you act today, ask, "What does His Word say?"
PRO 1:7.p: God is the final authority and has the final say in my life. I choose to fear and trust God and His Word!

1TI 5:8.o: God calls us to be our brother’s keeper. The world may try to communicate a narrative that you don’t have to worry about anyone but yourself, but the truth is that God designed a world that runs off serving, sacrifice, generosity, and love.
1TI 5:8.a: Take care of the people God has put in your life. Do something practical today for your family, a friend, or someone in need.
1TI 5:8.p: I am a producer and provider for those in my life whom God has called me to serve.

MRK 5:18-19.o: God has saved you and set you free, and now it’s your turn to go into your world and tell others the story of the goodness of God. Many people in your world may not come to church initially, but they can hear about Jesus and how He saves from you.
MRK 5:18-19.a: Tell your story. Share with one person this week what Jesus has done for you, or invite them to church.
MRK 5:18-19.p: I will tell the story of God’s goodness and salvation in my life to the world around me.

ACT 1:8.o: Jesus didn’t just save us from sin and leave us powerless on our own; He sent us the Holy Spirit. When you are filled and baptized with the Holy Spirit, you’ll receive power, peace, wisdom, and all the fruit of the Spirit.
ACT 1:8.a: Ask the Holy Spirit to fill you with power today. Then look for one person you can tell about Jesus this week.
ACT 1:8.p: I am filled with the Holy Spirit and will share my faith.

EXO 15:3.o: We were created in the image of a Warrior! Being a warrior doesn’t always mean being violent, but anyone who is a warrior is willing to do whatever is necessary to protect and defend those they love—even to their own pain.
EXO 15:3.a: Face today with courage. Remember that the Lord fights for you, and take one step toward what you've been afraid of.
EXO 15:3.p: The Lord is a Warrior, and so am I! I will face the valleys and the mountains with courage.

PRO 24:5-6.o: Wisdom unlocks your power and potential. Many men try to push and strive their way through to victory, but those who are wise will listen to counsel, coaching, and advice that will allow them to unlock their giftings and abilities.
PRO 24:5-6.a: Seek wise counsel before your next big decision. Call a mentor today and ask for their advice.
PRO 24:5-6.p: I will lead with wisdom and courage! I will seek the coaching of mentors before I charge into battle.

REV 11:15.o: As we wrap up this book, it’s important to know that God has an ultimate plan to evict evil from the earth and reestablish His kingdom across the planet! Jesus won our salvation on the cross, and He will have the final victory over the devil and end his rule on earth once and for all.
REV 11:15.a: Live today in light of His coming kingdom. Do one thing that points people toward Jesus the King.
REV 11:15.p: There is one King, and His name is Jesus. He will reign and restore all the nations of the earth to Himself.

EPH 4:32.o: Forgiving someone who wronged you can often feel like something that they must earn or deserve, but Jesus calls us to radical forgiveness; showing grace towards others even when they don’t deserve it.
EPH 4:32.a: Forgive someone today, as God forgave you. Name the person, release the offense in prayer, and show them kindness.
EPH 4:32.p: I am thankful for the mercy of God that forgave my sin. I choose to forgive those who have wronged me.

ACT 2:1-4.o: The Holy Spirit is not just some little voice on your shoulder trying to help you make better decisions; He is the Spirit of God! The Holy Spirit wants to empower and fill your life.
ACT 2:1-4.a: Invite the Holy Spirit to fill you today. Ask Him to lead, empower, and speak to you in every area of your life.
ACT 2:1-4.p: Holy Spirit, I invite you to come and fill every area of my life.

PHP 4:13.o: In the old cartoon, Popeye, he would get strength from eating spinach. But, for you and I, our strength to overcome is found in the strength that Jesus provides. And since we serve the God of the impossible that means that nothing is impossible if God has called you to do it.
PHP 4:13.a: Speak faith over your fears today. Say, "I can do all things through Christ," and take one step you've been avoiding.
PHP 4:13.p: I will not speak fear when God has called me to faith. I will speak in alignment with God’s Word about my life and calling.

JOB 13:14-16.o: Job is a man in the Bible who was very prosperous but experienced severe trials and lost everything, including his family. The journey Job walks through is almost unimaginable! Yet through it all, he maintains an unshakable view of God’s ultimate goodness.
JOB 13:14-16.a: Trust God even when you don't understand. Remember a time He was good to you, and put your hope in Him again today.
JOB 13:14-16.p: I will put my hope in God even when I don’t understand everything He’s doing.

JAS 1:2-3.o: A tree that has to grow with the wind pushing against it tends to be strong because its roots go down deep. The resistance makes it grow stronger, which is why James encouraged us to consider the trials of life a joy. That’s a bold statement! Pressure calls the strength out of you.
JAS 1:2-3.a: Face trials as a chance to grow. Ask God what He's teaching you in your current difficulty, and respond with joy.
JAS 1:2-3.p: God is using the difficulties in life to shape me for His purpose. I will embrace trials with joy!

1JN 4:4.o: What are you made of? This is a massive question! As children of God, we don’t have to answer this in our own strength or ability but in our God-given identity. What we have in us is greater than what’s in the world! What we have in us has overcome the enemy!
1JN 4:4.a: Remember who lives in you. When fear or pressure shows up, say, "The One in me is greater," and take courage.
1JN 4:4.p: I am a child of God, made in His image! With God, I will overcome every challenge.

JHN 14:27.o: Peace! What a beautiful word; it feels like most of the world is chasing peace but often missing out on it. Why? Because we’re seeking peace from the wrong source.
JHN 14:27.a: Receive Jesus' peace today. Give Him your anxiety, and look for peace in His presence instead of in circumstances.
JHN 14:27.p: Jesus, I receive your peace! Nothing on earth can take my joy. I will put my trust in you!

MRK 11:24.o: Jesus shows us the heart of God to engage and respond to us. First, He calls us to pray and ask Him for things. Don’t assume you’re bothering God, because your heavenly Father loves you and wants to respond. Then Jesus calls us to the next level by challenging us to believe.
MRK 11:24.a: Ask God boldly for something today. Pray it with faith, and keep believing as you wait.
MRK 11:24.p: In faith, I will boldly ask God for my needs and desires.

EPH 4:29.o: Our words are a powerful and creative force in our lives and the lives of those around us! When you constantly let harsh and cutting words come out of your mouth it is literally like going into the middle of a forest and then starting that forest on fire.
EPH 4:29.a: Speak life today. Before you say something harsh, pause. Encourage someone out loud and apologize if you need to.
EPH 4:29.p: My words have life or death. I will choose to make my words life and strength to others.

JHN 13:35.o: Your faith isn’t supposed to be hidden or silent. There are many ways that our faith is made public, and how you love others is one of those key factors.
JHN 13:35.a: Let your love be seen. Do something kind for a friend or stranger today as a way of showing Jesus' love.
JHN 13:35.p: I will live a life of love! I will love, honor, and encourage my friends and those in my world.

GEN 2:7.o: Our God is the most incredible designer; everywhere you look, creation is a megaphone for His power, creativity, and goodness. However, His best work is humanity. You were formed uniquely in His likeness; you carry an authority that no other creation has. God formed you to create, lead, and produce.
GEN 2:7.a: You were made in God's image. Create something today, or spend time asking God about your purpose.
GEN 2:7.p: I am created in the image of God. I carry His authority and power. I live with purpose and intention.

MAT 4:19.o: This is the greatest and most incredible call in the Bible, to Follow Jesus! It’s what Jesus said to His disciples and it’s the same call that comes to each of us. First, the call is to come close to him, to walk with him to be near him to have a restored relationship.
MAT 4:19.a: Say yes to Jesus' call to follow Him. Ask Him where He is leading you now, and take one step of obedience.
MAT 4:19.p: I hear Jesus calling me to follow and I will respond with a massive yes! Wherever God calls me I will go!

COL 2:12.o: Jesus was baptized in water, and we as believers are called to follow His example and get water baptized. This means to be fully submerged underneath the water. Why? Because we are symbolically representing Jesus’ death, burial, and resurrection.
COL 2:12.a: If you haven't been baptized, talk with your pastor about it this week. If you have, remember that you're alive in Jesus and leave your old life behind.
COL 2:12.p: I am a follower of Jesus. I am dead to my old life of sin and alive to Jesus and His purpose!

PHP 4:8.o: This is one of the greatest formulas in the Bible that will unlock God’s best for you. Learning to shift and choose what you consistently focus on will transform your life. Our thoughts are a primary driver of our emotions and our actions.
PHP 4:8.a: Take your thoughts captive today. Choose one thing that's true, pure, or lovely, and focus on it whenever worry creeps in.
PHP 4:8.p: I will choose to focus on what is good.

JOS 1:9.o: We are commanded by God to be strong and courageous. Why? Because life can be overwhelming, and it’s a choice to live with courage. The difficult seasons that we face are going to constantly try to drain our strength. Don’t be caught off guard by the challenges of life.
JOS 1:9.a: Be strong and courageous. Name what feels overwhelming and take one brave step today, knowing God is with you.
JOS 1:9.p: I will not be afraid or discouraged by my circumstances; I will put my confidence in Jesus and boldly take action!

1TH 4:1.o: The more you walk with Jesus, the more you’ll want to please Him with your life. It’s not something you’ll feel obligated to do; it’s just the natural response to His grace and goodness in your life.
1TH 4:1.a: Grow in your faith today. Pick one habit, like prayer, Bible reading, or generosity, and do it to please Jesus.
1TH 4:1.p: I will keep growing my faith and live to please God.!

ACT 4:30-31.o: God’s arm is not too short to reach into your situation and display His power. The Bible is clear that all things are possible with God; it’s God who heals, but His power is released by faith through us who believe.
ACT 4:30-31.a: Pray boldly for God to stretch out His hand. Ask Him for healing, provision, or deliverance for someone today.
ACT 4:30-31.p: Father, in Jesus' name, stretch out your hand to provide, heal, and deliver!

LUK 9:23.o: Being a Christian isn’t a multiple-choice box that you check on a heavenly entrance exam but then live your life however you want. Because He gave everything on the cross for us, we now live fully surrendered to His will and purpose.
LUK 9:23.a: Surrender something today. Ask Jesus what you need to lay down, and take up your cross to follow Him.
LUK 9:23.p: Jesus, I will lay down my life and pick up my cross daily to follow you and fulfill your mission.

PSA 119:43.o: King David knew how essential God’s Word is. So much so that he says, “Never take your word from my mouth.” The way he describes his hope in God’s Word is powerful. He knows where to put his hope. Often we’re caught in trouble because we’re putting our hope and trust in all the wrong things.
PSA 119:43.a: Speak God's Word out loud today. Choose one verse and say it over your day.
PSA 119:43.p: God’s Word is powerful and gives me hope! I will daily speak the truth from the Bible.

EPH 6:12.o: Did you know that the evil and dark forces trying to destroy you, aren’t just for theatrics in a movie? There is a real devil who hates God and therefore hates all who follow Him. So, there are going to be times when demonic presence is trying to work against you.
EPH 6:12.a: Remember your battle is spiritual. Pray today over the pressure you face, using God's power and the name of Jesus instead of your own strength.
EPH 6:12.p: There is an enemy but I do not need to fight him by natural means but in the power of God!

MAT 12:20-22.o: Jesus is the hope of all people in all nations. He is and always will be the true and only solution to the brokenness of mankind. But Jesus’ sacrifice is sufficient for everyone.
MAT 12:20-22.a: Put your hope in the God of justice and mercy. Pick one need in your city and ask how you can bring Jesus' hope to it.
MAT 12:20-22.p: I will put my hope in the God of justice and mercy!

MAT 9:27-30.o: These blind men knew that the messiah was coming from King David’s line, so when they call him son of David, they are affirming His power and authority! What are you saying about who Jesus is? Also, notice that Jesus asks the men if they believe He can heal them.
MAT 9:27-30.a: Come to Jesus with confidence that He is able and willing. Name the healing you need and ask in faith.
MAT 9:27-30.p: Jesus, I believe that you are the Messiah! I trust that you are able and willing to heal and deliver!

ROM 8:24.o: We’re being challenged here—in a good way! The Apostle Paul, who wrote this verse, is saying that if your hope is in just what you can see in the natural world, that’s not true hope and faith. Hope is a trust in the God of the universe’s ability to keep His Word.
ROM 8:24.a: Check what your hope rests on. If it's only circumstances, shift it to God's faithfulness and thank Him for one promise you can't yet see.
ROM 8:24.p: My hope isn’t built on circumstances but on God’s faithfulness.

1CO 16:13-14.o: We are called to operate in strength and authority, but the great Apostle Paul called us to top off all of our courage and strength with love. True masculinity as God designed it knows how to be strong, but also to love strong. We are courageous because of love, not in spite of it.
1CO 16:13-14.a: Be strong and courageous, and do everything in love. Name one fear to push past today, and one person to treat with kindness.
1CO 16:13-14.p: I am a man of courage who pushes past fear to walk in faith! I will do everything in love.

MRK 3:1-5.o: You’d think this was a rhetorical question: is doing good or evil lawful? But they couldn’t answer the question because it challenged their stubborn unbelief. So, Jesus overrides their religious pre-conceived ideas about good and evil and brings healing to the man suffering.
MRK 3:1-5.a: Never stop believing Jesus still heals. Today, pray for someone who is sick and ask Him to touch them.
MRK 3:1-5.p: Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever! He was and is our healer!

ISA 40:28.o: The Bible says that the joy of the Lord is our strength (Nehemiah 8:10). Hope is in the same vein as joy. When our hope disappears, we’ll find ourselves tired and losing the strength, both physically and mentally, to take on the adventures and challenges of life.
ISA 40:28.a: When you're weary, wait on the Lord. Take a few minutes today to rest in Him and ask Him to renew your strength.
ISA 40:28.p: I may get weary, but my strength will be renewed as I put my hope in God!

PSA 130:7.o: Are you calling others to hope? There’s a lot packed into this verse, but let’s focus on the fact that King David is directing and challenging his nation to put their hope in God.
PSA 130:7.a: Encourage someone to hope in God today. Send a text or share a verse with a friend who needs it.
PSA 130:7.p: I will call people to put their hope in the unfailing love of God!

1CO 10:13.o: The devil will bring temptations into your life that he knows to have the potential to derail you and cause you to sin. But, God’s word promises that He will always provide a way out of that situation.
1CO 10:13.a: Know your weak spots and plan an exit. Decide in advance what you'll do when temptation shows up, and take the way out God provides.
1CO 10:13.p: I choose to follow God’s way. When I’m tempted, with God’s help I’ll choose the way of life.

1CO 13:1-8.o: Our relationships thrive on love and hope. True love always hopes for the best and wants the best for you. When the people in your life can sense that you are believing the best about them and hoping for good for them, it’s an empowering and freeing thing. Have you lost hope for a friend?
1CO 13:1-8.a: Hope the best about the people in your life. Choose to speak life over one person today.
1CO 13:1-8.p: I will choose to hope and believe the best about the people in my life. I will speak life over them!

HEB 11:1.o: Hope is the vehicle that faith rides in on. Hope is the atmosphere for faith, and faith brings heaven to earth. What are you hoping for right now? What are you stretching for in faith? God wants you to trust Him for the dream, calling, and promises that are beyond your reach.
HEB 11:1.a: Name what you're hoping for and let it feed your faith. Pray with confidence that Jesus is the reason you hope.
HEB 11:1.p: Hope is the foundation of faith, and Jesus is the reason for my hope.

LUK 4:40-41.o: If you’re sick or hurting from any ailment, come to Jesus! We don’t always know what to do or how we’re going to make it through, but decide now that your first move will always be to bring it to Jesus!
LUK 4:40-41.a: Come to Jesus with whatever ails you today. Pray over your health or someone else's, and believe He cares.
LUK 4:40-41.p: Jesus, you are the healer of every kind of sickness! Nothing is beyond your care and power!

REV 3:20.o: Jesus gives us a window into the heart of God for us. First, Jesus wants to come into your life. He doesn’t want to stay as a distant spectator; He wants to be personally engaged in your world. He also shows that we have to invite Him in. He’s knocking on the door; only you can choose to open it.
REV 3:20.a: Open the door to Jesus. Invite Him into every area of your life today, especially the rooms you've kept closed.
REV 3:20.p: Jesus, you are welcome into every area of my life.

JHN 14:12.o: Jesus wants you and me to boldly carry out the mission He gave us and walk in the full power and authority that He walked in. Jesus even goes as far as to say that we’ll do even greater works! I want you to fully embrace the bigness of this idea!
JHN 14:12.a: Believe Jesus meant it. Ask Him for boldness to step out in faith and pray for someone today, trusting His power.
JHN 14:12.p: I choose to believe! His power is available to those who believe and step out in faith!

2CO 3:17.o: Freedom is at the core of Christianity. When you see and experience freedom you know that God is in it. Wherever freedom is growing it means that Biblical principles are at play. But when there’s a restricting and controlling state, it means the devil is at work.
2CO 3:17.a: Invite the Holy Spirit in, and make room for Him to bring freedom. Ask Him where you need it most today.
2CO 3:17.p: The Holy Spirit brings freedom everywhere He is. I will not control but empower.

ROM 3:23-24.o: Adam and Eve chose to disobey God, and as a result we are all born into sin. The culture says, “Everyone is basically good,” but the Bible says all have sinned and need a Savior.
ROM 3:23-24.a: Thank Jesus that you don't have to stay in sin. Receive His forgiveness today, and tell someone who needs a Savior.
ROM 3:23-24.p: I was born into sin, but thank God I don’t have to stay in sin. I am free and forgiven because of Jesus.

PSA 147:11.o: When you decide to honor and fear the Lord, it sets the rest of your life in order. The book of Proverbs teaches us that trusting the Lord is the beginning of wisdom (Proverbs 9:10). The words *hope* and *trust* are strongly linked.
PSA 147:11.a: Honor the Lord first today. Choose to trust His Word over your own opinions, and put your hope in His unfailing love.
PSA 147:11.p: I will submit my life fully to God! His ways are higher and more reliable than mine. My hope is in His love.

ACT 3:2-8.o: As followers of Christ, we carry something from Jesus that we have the authority to give away. We’ve received power from Him, and we have the ability to release it. Peter and John said, “What we have.”
ACT 3:2-8.a: Give away what God gave you. Ask Him who needs your prayer today, and offer it freely.
ACT 3:2-8.p: Jesus, we will freely release the power of God to others that you’ve given to us! Lord, increase our faith!

MAL 3:10.o: When praying for financial provision or breakthrough, it’s vital to ask the honor and tithing questions. Are you honoring God with the first 10% of all that you make? If you’re a tither, you can claim the promises and pray in alignment with the open heaven over your lives.
MAL 3:10.a: Pray with honor: give God your first and best from your income. Then ask for provision, standing on His promise.
MAL 3:10.p: I will honor the Lord in faithfully bringing my tithes! I will stand on his promise of blessing and protection!

PSA 119:9-11.o: Purity isn’t often a word we hear a lot about in normal conversations but God calls us to live with purity. The Bible calls us to sexual purity by keeping sex within the boundaries of marriage.
PSA 119:9-11.a: Guard your heart today by deciding on one boundary that protects your purity, then hide God's Word in your heart.
PSA 119:9-11.p: I will live with sexual purity in thought and in action. I will live according to Your Word.

ROM 12:1-2.o: What patterns are you building your life on? Every home needs blueprints for the crew to review and build from, and each of us is building our lives based on a set of patterns or blueprints.
ROM 12:1-2.a: Offer yourself to God as a living sacrifice today. Compare one habit to Scripture, and change it if it doesn't match.
ROM 12:1-2.p: I will give my life as a living sacrifice to God! I will not live for myself, but for Jesus and His kingdom.

JAS 1:22.o: It’s not good enough to just know what the Bible says. Even the devil knows what the Bible says and he most likely knows it more than you do. The real power of God’s Word is released when we act on it. Don’t be someone who comes to church and doesn’t apply it.
JAS 1:22.a: Don't just read the Bible; do it. Choose one thing God has shown you and take action on it today.
JAS 1:22.p: I will listen and obey God’s Word fully. When I follow God’s Words it unlocks all of God’s promises!

EPH 6:13-18.o: When a soldier goes into a battle, they make sure to put on their armor and choose their weapons. In the same way, we are in a spiritual battle and must armor up. Satan wants to stop God’s plans and cause damage to God’s people, but we have been given powerful weapons and armor.
EPH 6:13-18.a: Put on your armor today. Pick one verse to speak when temptation comes, because the Word is your sword.
EPH 6:13-18.p: Jesus has given me authority over the devil. God gave us armor to defend against the devil’s attacks and gave us weapons to defeat him.

PHP 4:6.o: It’s so easy to rush into fear! It’s common to second guess yourself and even question God if we allow anxious thoughts to overtake and set up camp in our minds. We know anxious thoughts will come, but we don’t have to dwell on them. It says don’t be anxious but pray.
PHP 4:6.a: Turn your worry into prayer today. Name each anxious thought to God, thank Him, and ask Him for peace.
PHP 4:6.p: I will not live in fear; I will turn the attention of my mind and heart towards God and His goodness!

PSA 147:3.o: Jesus cares about the things that have wounded your soul. He sees the traumas that have left you feeling hurt and injured mentally and emotionally.
PSA 147:3.a: Let Jesus heal what hurts. Bring Him an old wound today and ask Him to restore your soul.
PSA 147:3.p: Lord, heal my heart, set me free from the pain of the past, and restore my soul so I can walk in peace.

JHN 14:6.o: The culture around you is often confused about what is true or even if we’re able to know what truth is. But, know that there are absolute truths revealed in nature and confirmed by God in the Bible. There is truth and lies. There’s right and wrong.
JHN 14:6.a: Hold to Jesus as the only way and share that with love. Pray today for a friend who doesn't know Him.
JHN 14:6.p: Jesus is the only way to Heaven! God’s Word is the final truth and authority we live our lives by!

PSA 91:1-2.o: Do you or someone you know need rest? Do you need peace? You’ll find that when you rest in the shadow or presence of God. When you’re spending time in the presence of God through prayer, worship, and the Word, you’ll find that peace comes.
PSA 91:1-2.a: Dwell in God's presence today. Take time to be still, and trust Him with what weighs on you.
PSA 91:1-2.p: God, I put my trust in you! I will rest in your presence and find hope as I wait on you!

ROM 8:28.o: No matter what you’re facing, as a child of God, you can be confident that He is actively working all the good and the bad circumstances for your good.
ROM 8:28.a: Trust that God is working in your situation. Thank Him today for one hard thing, believing He will use it for good.
ROM 8:28.p: God is good and working good for me! I will trust Him in all circumstances!

1PE 2:24.o: Do you need healing? Are you sick? Jesus took all of our sins, sicknesses, and diseases on himself and put them to death on the cross. Jesus made the advanced payment for our sin and disease; now, we must learn to walk it out.
1PE 2:24.a: Thank Jesus for taking your sin and sickness on the cross. Receive His healing today, and pray for someone else who needs it.
1PE 2:24.p: Jesus has paid for my salvation and healing! Through His death on the cross, we now live free and healed!

JOS 24:15.o: Part of your role as a man is to stand against the lies, mediocrity, and pressures that the enemy and culture send your way.
JOS 24:15.a: Choose today who you will serve. Lead your family in one act of worship, such as prayer, Scripture, or thanks.
JOS 24:15.p: As for me and my family, we will serve the Lord!

PHP 1:6.o: As men, we’re born to compete and conquer! This is why we get discouraged when we focus too much on what we’re not, or on what we haven’t achieved yet. Allow this verse to breathe peace into your soul; you can be confident that if God began a good work in you, He will be faithful to complete it.
PHP 1:6.a: Stop comparing. Thank God for what He's already done in you, and trust Him to finish what He started.
PHP 1:6.p: God, thank you for all that you’ve done in my life. You will finish in me what you started.

PSA 107:19-21.o: The power of God is released in His Word! He sent His Word and healed them! He’s still doing the same today! He’s the healer and redeemer of His people! We are on the receiving end of His words of life, and we are privileged by God to be the ones who release His Word as well!
PSA 107:19-21.a: Pray God's Word over your need today. Ask Him to send His Word and heal, and thank Him in advance.
PSA 107:19-21.p: Lord, you hear our cry for help! Now, send your Word and Heal! I will give you all the praise and glory!

PSA 9:17-19.o: God is the hope of the afflicted! God isn’t just interested in you when you win and are on top of the world.
PSA 9:17-19.a: God never forgets the hurting. Bring Him your loss or failure today, and ask Him to remind you that you are not forgotten.
PSA 9:17-19.p: Even if I fail, God will protect me and never forget me.
