GEN 1:26.o: You are not just an evolved animal or a cosmic explosion; you have been intentionally handcrafted by God to be in relationship with Him. No other being on earth has that honor. This is why we refer to God as our heavenly Father, because He created us.
GEN 1:26.a: Remember you were made in God's image. Live today like it, with purpose, dignity, and love for others.
GEN 1:26.p: I am a child of God and carry His name. I walk out His mission here on earth.

PRO 30:5.o: God’s Word is not just good ideas or interesting stories. The Bible gives us complete and perfect wisdom for life. Throughout the last several thousand years, scientific, historical, and psychological discoveries continue to echo and prove Biblical accuracy.
PRO 30:5.a: Let God's Word shield you today. Read one verse before you open your phone, and trust it more than the headlines.
PRO 30:5.p: God’s Words are perfect. I will live according to The Bible’s instruction.

MAT 4:23-24.o: How incredible that Jesus healed and delivered all those who came to Him! Jesus came preaching the Kingdom and began to cast out all that wasn’t in alignment with His will. We’re called to be ambassadors of His Kingdom!
MAT 4:23-24.a: Pray for healing and freedom in Jesus' name. Ask Him to bring His Kingdom into one situation today.
MAT 4:23-24.p: Jesus heals and delivers everyone who comes to Him! In your name, we’ll establish your Kingdom!

JAS 1:5.o: The Bible says He will generously give you wisdom. The Holy Spirit is our guide, comforter, and leader. He’s wanting to guide you along the path of truth. Don’t try to struggle and push your way through life without asking for help from God. He’s available to you and wants to speak to you.
JAS 1:5.a: Ask God for wisdom today, since He gives generously. Bring Him one decision and listen for His answer.
JAS 1:5.p: God is willing and ready to guide and give me wisdom on all occasions.

PRO 3:5-6.o: When we submit our life decisions to God, we find that things begin to straighten out. We can get caught in cycles of dysfunction because we’re stuck in a rut of doing what has always been done even though it’s not working.
PRO 3:5-6.a: Bring your decision to God before you act. Where your own thinking has been unreliable, lean on His Word instead.
PRO 3:5-6.p: I will trust God’s Word over my own. I will be stable and unshakable as I lean on His truth.

COL 3:20.o: God has entrusted parents with the amazing responsibility to care for, protect and teach their children. And as a child, when you honor your parents and follow their instructions you’ll find a blessing in that and God’s grace on it.
COL 3:20.a: Honor your parents today with a kind word, a thank-you, or a chore done without being asked.
COL 3:20.p: I love and honor my parents. I will obey my parents and grow up to be a great parent that shows my kids God’s ways.

NUM 13:30.o: We will conclude by reading about the courage of Caleb. The other ten spies were convincing Moses and the Israelites that the Promised Land was too dangerous and the people too strong. Then Caleb stepped up, challenged their fear, and called the people to believe the promises of God again!
NUM 13:30.a: Choose courage over fear today. Encourage someone who's afraid to take the step God is calling them toward.
NUM 13:30.p: With God, we can and will fulfill all that He has called us to accomplish!

PRO 13:12.o: Many are disheartened and discouraged because of unfulfilled hopes and dreams. But we see clearly that God loves to see your desires fulfilled. You’re not fighting against God to do and accomplish what’s in your heart; you’re working with Him.
PRO 13:12.a: Bring your hopes to God today, those fulfilled and those delayed. Thank Him for one, and trust Him with the other.
PRO 13:12.p: I will thank God for hopes fulfilled, and I will trust God when dreams are delayed.

PRO 11:24-25.o: God’s kingdom flows through giving. Jesus said it’s more blessed to give than to receive. When we posture our lives in a giving, serving mode it will expand and unlock our life. Many people live in fear of losing. Maybe losing money, or friends, or influence or their career.
PRO 11:24-25.a: Be generous today. Give to someone as a surprise, whether it's money, time, or kindness, and see what God does.
PRO 11:24-25.p: I will live a big and generous life. I will focus more on giving than receiving.

1TH 4:3-5.o: The world will try to tell you that we need to follow our impulses and desires, but God gives us the Holy Spirit to help us produce self-control. Because of our sinful nature, we will be pulled toward sin.
1TH 4:3-5.a: Honor God with your body and your thoughts. Choose one boundary today that helps you walk in purity and self-control.
1TH 4:3-5.p: I will honor God by living in sexual purity.

JAS 1:2-4.o: A tree that has to grow with the wind pushing against it tends to be strong because its roots go down deep. The resistance makes it grow stronger, which is why James encouraged us to consider the trials of life a joy. That’s a bold statement! Pressure calls the strength out of you.
JAS 1:2-4.a: Face trials as a chance to grow. Ask God what He's teaching you in your current difficulty, and respond with joy.
JAS 1:2-4.p: God is using the difficulties in life to shape me for His purpose. I will embrace trials with joy!

PRO 27:18.o: In a world of self-promotion, God’s word calls us to something different. This Proverb holds a major key to life and success. Instead of your primary focus being how you can get ahead or how others can help you, look to see first how you can serve and help someone else’s dream come to pass.
PRO 27:18.a: Help someone else's dream come true. Ask a leader or friend how you can serve their vision today.
PRO 27:18.p: I will look to fulfill the vision of those God has put in my life first. As I honor others, honor will flow to me.

HEB 11:6.o: Without faith, it’s impossible to please God. Faith is the currency of heaven. It’s the conduit for bringing things from heaven to earth. It pleases God because faith is believing He is who He says He is, and it’s drawing on Him in faith for the unseen or the impossible.
HEB 11:6.a: Pray a bold prayer of faith today, or pick up one you stopped praying. Believe God rewards those who seek Him.
HEB 11:6.p: God, I trust you and put my faith in you. You will fulfill what you said you would do.

ROM 5:8.o: God always goes first. He loves first, He forgives first! And Jesus displays the most unreal heart of God by dying on the cross for us even before we chose to follow Him. That’s how valuable you are to Him that He was willing to leave heaven and risk it all to bring you close to Himself again.
ROM 5:8.a: God loved you first. Thank Him for it today, and show kindness to someone who hasn't earned it.
ROM 5:8.p: Thank you, Jesus, for dying for me even while I was against you and now I follow and surrendered to you.

MAT 6:33.o: God has established order and priorities within the kingdom of God, and when you put the right things in the proper order, you’ll experience a greater flow and blessing.
MAT 6:33.a: Seek God's Kingdom first today. Before anything else, give Him your first thought, your first hour, or your first effort.
MAT 6:33.p: I will build and advance the kingdom of God on earth with my life, work, and relationships.

HEB 6:18-20.o: Hope is an anchor! An anchor grounds us, stabilizes us, and keeps us from being tossed back and forth by the wind and the waves. We can be tossed by things above and below the surface, but the anchor holds us securely. Today, get your life anchored in Christ. How?
HEB 6:18-20.a: Let hope anchor you. When life tosses you around today, hold on to Jesus' promises and don't drift.
HEB 6:18-20.p: I am secure because my hope is anchored in Jesus!

PRO 11:7.o: Where is your hope placed today? Is it in the temporary or the eternal? Often to get the right view of something, we have to elevate our perspective. We need to see it from above. When you’re down in the weeds of life, it’s easy to get overwhelmed and to lose sight of where you’re going.
PRO 11:7.a: Lift your view today. Ask whether your hope is in something temporary or eternal, and shift it to God.
PRO 11:7.p: God, you are sure and reliable! When I trust you, I won’t be disappointed.

LUK 10:27.o: The strength of a man flows from his connection to his heavenly Father. Jesus reminded us that our primary focus must be to love and honor God with our lives. It’s the thing that should guide and govern our choices.
LUK 10:27.a: Love God with everything today, then let that love flow into someone around you. Ask what honors Him in how you spend your time.
LUK 10:27.p: I will love God with all my heart, soul, strength, and mind! Love for others flows from loving God.

MAT 7:24.o: What foundation are you building your life on? Jesus calls us to build on the only sure and solid foundation, which is His Word. Following the ideas and thoughts from this world is like building your house on a shaky and uncertain foundation.
MAT 7:24.a: Choose one area that feels shaky and rebuild it on God's Word. Memorize one verse and put it into action this week.
MAT 7:24.p: My life will be built on the foundation of God’s Word.

MAT 10:1.o: This verse should stir your faith massively! Jesus, our all-powerful Savior and Lord, allows and commissions us to release His power by delegating His authority to us! You don’t heal through good vibes or well wishes; you must learn to take your God-given authority and drive out the enemy.
MAT 10:1.a: Believe Jesus has given you authority in His name. Pray with confidence over a sickness or struggle today.
MAT 10:1.p: I have been entrusted with authority over demons and all diseases through the name of Jesus and will use it!

MAT 17:14-18.o: Healing and deliverance is an act of mercy; we should never see someone suffering and not want to extend our hand to bring freedom. That is always the heart of God. This man and the disciples can’t get his son set free.
MAT 17:14-18.a: Look for someone who is hurting and offer to pray. Ask God to remove any doubt that keeps you from reaching out.
MAT 17:14-18.p: Lord, I confess any sin or unbelief that’s holding me back from ministering healing and freedom!

1CO 16:13.o: We are called to operate in strength and authority, but the great Apostle Paul called us to top off all of our courage and strength with love. True masculinity as God designed it knows how to be strong, but also to love strong. We are courageous because of love, not in spite of it.
1CO 16:13.a: Be strong and courageous, and do everything in love. Name one fear to push past today, and one person to treat with kindness.
1CO 16:13.p: I am a man of courage who pushes past fear to walk in faith! I will do everything in love.

1PE 5:8.o: Yes, we have an enemy that roars like a lion, but the good news is he’s not a lion. He will try to scare and harass you and ultimately devour you if you let him. He’s looking for someone who’s not paying attention and is unaware of the uppercut that’s coming their way.
1PE 5:8.a: Stay alert today. Know where the enemy tends to attack you, and stand firm with prayer and the Word.
1PE 5:8.p: I am alert, aware, and ready to defeat the attacks of the enemy. I will stand firm in my faith and resist the enemy.

PRO 20:7.o: What you do and how you live matter. The choices that we as men make will impact those around us and will leave a legacy of strength or pain for our children. When we live righteously, which is in alignment with God’s Word, we’ll see our children blessed.
PRO 20:7.a: Live today the way you want your family to remember you. Choose integrity in one specific area, and ask God to help.
PRO 20:7.p: With God’s help, I will live a righteous and pure life. My wife, children, and friends will be blessed!

PSA 139:14.o: God created the whole world in all its glory and He hand-formed and created you. You weren’t just thrown together but wonderfully and specifically made. Made in His image and made with incredible value and purpose.
PSA 139:14.a: Thank God today that you are wonderfully made. Honor others as God's handiwork, and treat each person with dignity.
PSA 139:14.p: I will value my life and every human life. All people are hand-made by God in their mother’s womb with great intentionality and purpose.

ECC 4:9-12.o: We are designed by God for relationships. Having great people in your life isn’t just a nice idea; it’s essential for your development and for fulfilling your purpose and calling. Don’t try to be an island in life; don’t try to do it all alone.
ECC 4:9-12.a: Call a friend today. Ask for help where you're struggling, or offer help to someone else, because two are better than one.
ECC 4:9-12.p: Two are better than one. I will add value to others.

ROM 4:18.o: What a powerful verse! Against all odds, Abraham goes all in! Abraham was over eighty and had no children, but God promised to make a huge nation from his descendents and Abraham believed God! So now we know him as the father of the faith.
ROM 4:18.a: Hope against hope. Pick the promise God gave you and keep trusting Him, no matter what you see.
ROM 4:18.p: No matter what circumstances look like in the natural, I will put my hope in the promise-keeping God!

1PE 5:8-9.o: Yes, we have an enemy that roars like a lion, but the good news is he’s not a lion. He will try to scare and harass you and ultimately devour you if you let him. He’s looking for someone who’s not paying attention and is unaware of the uppercut that’s coming their way.
1PE 5:8-9.a: Stay alert today. Know where the enemy tends to attack you, and stand firm with prayer and the Word.
1PE 5:8-9.p: I am alert, aware, and ready to defeat the attacks of the enemy. I will stand firm in my faith and resist the enemy.

JAS 5:14-15.o: Is “anyone” sick? This may seem like a simple question, but the Bible is telling us that it’s the heart and desire of God to heal everyone who is sick. This is important since there will be some Christian circles that suggest that God doesn’t heal today or that we don’t know if God wants you healed.
JAS 5:14-15.a: If you're sick, ask for prayer. Call your pastor or a friend today and believe God for healing.
JAS 5:14-15.p: When I’m sick, I will engage my church community and believe for supernatural healing!

MAT 6:31-33.o: First things first! There’s an order to life. When things are in order and alignment they tend to work better. When you put God’s kingdom first, there’s less need to worry about your situation.
MAT 6:31-33.a: Put first things first. Give your worries to God today, and make His Kingdom your priority.
MAT 6:31-33.p: I will seek first His Kingdom and His will for my life! I will be blessed as I put His will first!

PSA 118:6-9.o: The Lord is with you! This truth will create peace and confidence through seasons where it feels like life and people are against you. The Bible reminds us that you don’t need to fear humans and what they can do to you; you just need to fear God and what He can do.
PSA 118:6-9.a: Remember that the Lord is with you. Replace one fear with this truth, and trust Him instead of people.
PSA 118:6-9.p: God is with me so I will not fear! I will put my hope and confidence in God.

MRK 1:40-41.o: I love this passage! Jesus is insulted by this person’s question. His indignation comes in response to someone questioning his heart and desire to free them from their suffering. His reaction is because His good plans for people are in question.
MRK 1:40-41.a: Know that Jesus is willing. Bring Him your need today, and believe that He wants to help you.
MRK 1:40-41.p: Jesus, you are good, and You do good things for your people! You are able and willing to heal and deliver!

EPH 2:12.o: The purest form of hopelessness isn’t that things are difficult but that Jesus is not present. No matter the circumstance, if God is with you, you don’t need to feel hopeless. If you’ve found Christ, then you’ve found pure hope.
EPH 2:12.a: With Jesus, there's always hope. Think of someone who doesn't know Him, and pray for them today.
EPH 2:12.p: I have great hope! Jesus paid the debt of my sin.

ROM 5:3-5.o: When you trust God, hope is an end product of life’s trials. Instead of these circumstances taking us out, they begin to produce perseverance and character that shape our hope. It says hope doesn’t disappoint. What does that mean?
ROM 5:3-5.a: Let your trials produce hope. Ask God what He's building in you, and stay faithful through today's difficulty.
ROM 5:3-5.p: Patience produces godly character and a sure hope!

MIC 6:8.o: In this verse, God gets super clear on the values that He wants us to live by. We must act justly. This means that we’re walking with integrity in all that we do and in how we treat others. Then we are to love mercy.
MIC 6:8.a: Act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly. Choose one of these three for today, and do it.
MIC 6:8.p: I will treat people fairly. I will extend forgiveness. I will honor God’s thoughts above my own.

PRO 24:14.o: We see here that hope is a by-product of wisdom. Hope is not a feeling that’s disconnected from reality; it’s a feeling and expectation that flows from a life of wisdom.
PRO 24:14.a: Ask God for wisdom, and expect hope to follow. Set time with a wise person this week for advice.
PRO 24:14.p: God, I will seek your wisdom and find hope!

EPH 1:20-23.o: Jesus is powerfully active on the earth today through the Church. The gathering of believers at church is not just a religious gathering but the active body and extension of Jesus here on earth! You are an essential part of the body of Jesus and His plan to seek and save the planet.
EPH 1:20-23.a: Be part of the Church. Take one step to get more involved this week, whether it's serving, giving, or inviting someone.
EPH 1:20-23.p: I am a vital part of the Church, fulfilling the mission Jesus gave us to accomplish.

PRO 27:17.o: When iron strikes iron, sparks begin to fly! It can be the same with us as men. When you’re in close connection and mentorship with another man, those times of discipleship and confrontation are the iron-striking-iron moments that cause us to be sharp.
PRO 27:17.a: Sharpen someone and be sharpened. Invite a friend or mentor to speak honestly into your life this week.
PRO 27:17.p: I will not avoid confrontation or correction. I will embrace the input of my friends and mentors so I can grow!

LUK 18:1-8.o: Persistence in prayer is what Jesus is calling us to! What are you believing for? What do you need God to do in your life? It’s time to be faithful to pray and continue in prayer until the answer has come.
LUK 18:1-8.a: Keep praying. Pick the one thing you've been believing for and pray about it again today without giving up.
LUK 18:1-8.p: I will pray and keep on praying until I see the victory!

ROM 3:23.o: Adam and Eve chose to disobey God, and as a result we are all born into sin. The culture says, “Everyone is basically good,” but the Bible says all have sinned and need a Savior.
ROM 3:23.a: Thank Jesus that you don't have to stay in sin. Receive His forgiveness today, and tell someone who needs a Savior.
ROM 3:23.p: I was born into sin, but thank God I don’t have to stay in sin. I am free and forgiven because of Jesus.

PSA 31:19.o: This is a powerful reminder of the good intentions of our heavenly Father. He has goodness stored up for you! He is the Good Shepherd, who will not leave you alone or abandon you but will give you an inheritance of His kingdom.
PSA 31:19.a: Believe your Father has good stored up for you. Ask Him for something specific today and thank Him in advance.
PSA 31:19.p: My heavenly Father has intentional and good plans for my future!

LUK 7:12-15.o: Jesus came to bring life in every sense of that word! He brought people back to life, and He rose from the dead to show that He was Lord over life and death. He conquered hell and the death. Jesus still brings dead things back to life!
LUK 7:12-15.a: Bring Jesus the dead and dry places in your life. Ask Him to breathe life into them today.
LUK 7:12-15.p: You are the life giver and restorer! You bring dead things back to life! You conquered death and the grave!

1TI 6:11-12.o: As a man after God’s heart, it’s not just about fleeing sin but about what we’re pursuing. All of the great men of faith in the Bible aren’t in there because they didn’t sin. As a matter of fact, there are some pretty horrific things that many of them did in their lives.
1TI 6:11-12.a: Don't just flee from sin, but pursue something. Choose one habit of righteousness, faith, or love, and set a boundary that protects it.
1TI 6:11-12.p: I hate sin and love God’s Word. I will live with purity, faith, and courage.

LUK 6:31.o: Our human instinct is to try and treat people the way they are treating us. If someone is rude or mean to us then we want to be mean back to them, but Jesus calls us to look past how we’re being treated and work to treat people how we would want them to treat us.
LUK 6:31.a: Treat someone well today, especially if they've treated you badly. Do for them what you'd want done for you.
LUK 6:31.p: I will treat others the way I want to be treated no matter how they are treating me.

LUK 17:17-19.o: Are you indifferent or thankful for God’s goodness? We may feel that’s an obvious yes, but it requires intentionality not to forget His blessings and move too quickly to familiarity.
LUK 17:17-19.a: Say thank you to God today, specifically. Write down three of His blessings and tell Him you're grateful.
LUK 17:17-19.p: Thank you, Lord, for your kindness, goodness, and justice! You’re the healer and restorer of my life!

ROM 10:9-10.o: Choosing to follow Jesus moves you from the kingdom of Satan to the kingdom of light!
ROM 10:9-10.a: If you haven't yet, confess Jesus as Lord out loud today. If you have, tell one person about your decision to follow Him.
ROM 10:9-10.p: I declare that Jesus is my Lord; I will live for Him.

PHP 4:6-7.o: It’s so easy to rush into fear! It’s common to second guess yourself and even question God if we allow anxious thoughts to overtake and set up camp in our minds. We know anxious thoughts will come, but we don’t have to dwell on them. It says don’t be anxious but pray.
PHP 4:6-7.a: Turn your worry into prayer today. Name each anxious thought to God, thank Him, and ask Him for peace.
PHP 4:6-7.p: I will not live in fear; I will turn the attention of my mind and heart towards God and His goodness!

PSA 65:5.o: This verse reminds us that He is an answering God. He’s not distant and silent and uninterested; He’s present and answering in abundant fashion. Also, notice that God is not just our hope in whatever nation you’re reading this, but God is the hope of all people in all nations.
PSA 65:5.a: Remember a prayer God answered. Thank Him for it today and bring Him the next one, believing He hears.
PSA 65:5.p: God loves to hear from me and will answer my prayer. You are the hope of the nations!

LUK 9:23-24.o: Being a Christian isn’t a multiple-choice box that you check on a heavenly entrance exam but then live your life however you want. Because He gave everything on the cross for us, we now live fully surrendered to His will and purpose.
LUK 9:23-24.a: Surrender something today. Ask Jesus what you need to lay down, and take up your cross to follow Him.
LUK 9:23-24.p: Jesus, I will lay down my life and pick up my cross daily to follow you and fulfill your mission.

LAM 3:20-22.o: If we’re going to be overflowing with hope, we have to learn how to call to mind the right things. We are constantly bombarded with the wrong thoughts and negative messaging that drain our strength.
LAM 3:20-22.a: Call to mind God's faithfulness today. Write down three ways His love has shown up, and let that fuel your hope.
LAM 3:20-22.p: The love of God is great and never-ending! I will put my hope in His faithfulness.

MAT 7:7-8.o: These verses remind us of two major factors: first, God wants you to ask and keep asking until the answer comes, and second, God wants to give us good things. How often do we quit and stop short in prayer because we get fatigued with the delays or assume God is uninterested?
MAT 7:7-8.a: Ask God for something specific today, and keep asking. Believe that your Father wants to give you good things.
MAT 7:7-8.p: God is good and loves to give us good things! I will ask according to His will and keep seeking and knocking until the answer comes!

MAT 9:35.o: A New Kingdom means a new King; with that new Lord comes new rules and ways of doing things. Jesus came to bring in a new Kingdom, which was more powerful than the previous one. The new kingdom brings life and hope, while the last kingdom is one of darkness and pain.
MAT 9:35.a: Live under the new King's rules today. Ask Jesus where His way differs from the world's, and follow His way.
MAT 9:35.p: I will proclaim the good news of your Kingdom! I will exercise the authority that you’ve given me!

1PE 1:3.o: Often when people talk about church, they think of religion and rules, but God calls us into a living and alive relationship with Him. Your salvation isn’t into a dead religion but a living hope. Have you ever been looking at an instruction manual and realized it’s for an older model of vehicle?
1PE 1:3.a: Your hope is alive because Jesus is alive. Thank Him for new life today, and let it ease your fear.
1PE 1:3.p: My hope is alive in Jesus! I do not fear because He is with me!

1CO 10:12-13.o: We’d all like to think we’re invincible against sin and temptation, but if we’re honest, we each have areas of potential weakness. Now, what the devil would like you to think is that you’re abnormal and alone in your temptations. The truth is that, like the Bible says, it’s common.
1CO 10:12-13.a: Don't think you're beyond temptation. Be honest with a trusted friend about where you struggle, and take the way out God provides.
1CO 10:12-13.p: I am not alone in my temptations. God has provided a way out, and with the help of my brothers in Christ, I will take it!

PSA 91:1.o: Do you or someone you know need rest? Do you need peace? You’ll find that when you rest in the shadow or presence of God. When you’re spending time in the presence of God through prayer, worship, and the Word, you’ll find that peace comes.
PSA 91:1.a: Dwell in God's presence today. Take time to be still, and trust Him with what weighs on you.
PSA 91:1.p: God, I put my trust in you! I will rest in your presence and find hope as I wait on you!

PRO 4:23.o: The Bible doesn’t make many of these statements of extreme importance. So, we want to take note when it says “above all.” We need to realize that all good and evil flows out of the heart. So, that means you want to be extra specific about what you allow to come into your heart.
PRO 4:23.a: Guard your heart today. Decide what you'll stop watching, listening to, or dwelling on, and replace it with God's Word.
PRO 4:23.p: Life flows from my heart! I will guard and protect it by using a Biblical filter on what I listen to, watch and do.

PSA 119:105.o: In this life, we can sometimes feel confused or uncertain about the next steps we should take. But that’s where God’s Word comes in. One of the ways to see the Bible is like a flashlight on the path of life.
PSA 119:105.a: Let God's Word light your next step. Read a short passage before your day starts and ask Him which direction to take.
PSA 119:105.p: God’s Word brings light and clarity to my daily decisions.

PSA 23:1.o: These are great verses to read often. It speaks of God’s desire to bring us peace and to lead us into good things. He desires that you lack nothing! These verses give us a promise, that no matter what dark and painful season we may be facing, God will never leave us.
PSA 23:1.a: Read Psalm 23 slowly today. Remember a hard time when God was still with you, and let that memory quiet your fear.
PSA 23:1.p: I will follow the leading of the Good Shepherd. I will not live in fear because He is with me!

PSA 42:5.o: King David ruled over ancient Israel and was known as a great writer of prayers and songs throughout his life. In this verse, King David articulates the battle of being led by our emotions rather than by God’s character. He asks a great question of himself: “Why are you so depressed?”
PSA 42:5.a: Talk to your soul like David did. When you feel downcast, say, "Put your hope in God," and thank Him for who He is.
PSA 42:5.p: I will not be led by my emotions; I will put my hope in God.

2CO 6:14.o: What does the Bible mean by yoked? It’s a term for the harness that goes over two animals plowing a field. To get the maximum potential out of the ox or horse you’ll need to select two animals that are similar in height so that they pull at similar strength.
2CO 6:14.a: Check your closest relationships. Ask whether they build up your faith, and invest more in friends who run toward Jesus.
2CO 6:14.p: I will choose the relationships that share my passion for Jesus, life, and calling.

DEU 31:6.o: What could possibly be stronger than God’s Word in your life? The answer is nothing! No matter who or what tries to come against you, take it with courage and peace, knowing that God’s promise is for you—He will never forsake you! He will not leave you alone or on your own.
DEU 31:6.a: Be strong and courageous. Remember that God goes with you, and face today's challenge knowing you're not alone.
DEU 31:6.p: I will be strong and face my purpose because God is going with me on this journey!

PSA 37:34.o: Great hope is found on God’s path. When we follow the Bible, we’ll find that we can be safe and secure in what we do. You may want to be hopeful, but if we don’t follow His path, we’ll find ourselves slipping.
PSA 37:34.a: Follow God's path today. Choose one place where you've been doing it your way and do it His way instead.
PSA 37:34.p: I will carefully live according to God’s ways. He will elevate and establish my life.

2TI 1:7.o: Since we know that God’s Spirit is greater than all other spirits on the planet, it should give you boldness and courage! Fear, insecurity, and intimidation are not a normal or acceptable part of Christianity.
2TI 1:7.a: Refuse fear today. Remember that God gave you power, love, and a sound mind, and take one bold step in faith.
2TI 1:7.p: I carry the Spirit of faith! I will not live in fear or be intimidated, but will act with courage!

GAL 5:22-25.o: Fruit is the product of a seed. In the same way, when we open up our lives and hearts to the Spirit of God, He’ll plant seeds of love, joy, peace, and all those qualities mentioned in Galatians 5:22-23. As we keep cultivating those seeds, we’ll find they begin to produce that same life in us.
GAL 5:22-25.a: Pick one fruit of the Spirit you need most today and ask Him to grow it. Plant good seeds by what you read, watch, and say.
GAL 5:22-25.p: I will walk in step with the Holy Spirit. As I follow the Holy Spirit, I will produce the fruit of the Spirit.

REV 21:4-5.o: We know that Jesus heals and that He came to bring the Kingdom of Heaven to Earth! In this life, we’re going to face trials, pain, sickness, and even death before our time. In this life, we’re going to take our stand against the work of the enemy, and we’ll experience both victories and defeats.
REV 21:4-5.a: Look forward to the day God makes all things new. Pray for the sick and hurting today, and let that promise give you hope.
REV 21:4-5.p: Jesus, we pray and work towards your soon return and the establishment of your Kingdom in full!

PSA 84:11.o: God is our protector and covering and he desires to release all of His goodness in your life. In the beginning, God created absolute perfection for Adam and Eve to live in, which gives us a window into the heart of God to always give His kids the best. God doesn’t withhold any good thing.
PSA 84:11.a: Walk in integrity today. Ask God for the goodness He promises, and live in a way that honors Him.
PSA 84:11.p: I will walk in the favor and honor the Lord provides. I will walk with integrity.

1TH 5:8.o: Hope is a helmet. Hope is an insulation against the mental attack of the enemy. One of the main ways that the enemy attacks us is through our minds—getting us to think in a way that is destructive to our lives and future.
1TH 5:8.a: Put on the helmet of hope. When negative thoughts attack today, answer with a promise from God.
1TH 5:8.p: God will guard my heart and mind as I put my hope in Him!

EPH 6:10-18.o: There is a spiritual battle between demonic forces and the followers of Jesus here on earth. It’s not hyperbole; it’s a real battle—but the good news is that God didn’t leave us without armor and weapons for this battle. Read all of Ephesians 6:10-18 to know all of the pieces of armor.
EPH 6:10-18.a: Put on God's armor today. Name the spiritual pressure you feel and stand firm against it with prayer and the Word.
EPH 6:10-18.p: I am equipped to fight and defeat the enemy.

MAT 10:8.o: It’s your turn! Often, people assume that seeing someone get healed is only what the pastors or people with a lot of faith do, but Jesus tells all his disciples to heal the sick! To raise the dead! To drive out demons! This is the work available to all followers of Jesus!
MAT 10:8.a: It's your turn. Pray for someone who needs healing, trusting that Jesus gave you His authority.
MAT 10:8.p: I have power and authority over the enemy! I will bring freedom and healing in Jesus’ name!

1JN 4:19.o: I’m so thankful for this truth! God didn’t come to you and love you because you earned it or proved you were good enough for His love. He came to earth and died on the cross because He loved us! Jesus went first! And the love and grace and forgiveness we have all flow because He loves us.
1JN 4:19.a: Receive God's love today. You didn't earn it, and you can't lose it. Pass it on by loving one person without expecting anything back.
1JN 4:19.p: I am loved by God. I will love others as Jesus loves me.

ROM 8:1.o: This is one of the really good news verses in the Bible. Because of what Jesus did by taking on the punishment of our sin, we don’t have to live under shame and condemnation for our sin that we have confessed to Jesus.
ROM 8:1.a: Let go of your shame and regret. Confess to Jesus, receive His forgiveness, and walk as someone with no condemnation.
ROM 8:1.p: In Jesus, I am forgiven and free! I don’t need to live in regret or shame. I am a child of God!

GEN 2:19.o: One of the first things God did with Adam before He brought Eve into his life was to teach him to name the animals. Whatever Adam called them, that was their name. It’s similar in our lives. God is going to teach you the power of the words you use and the labels that you put on people.
GEN 2:19.a: Use your words well today. Speak a blessing, name a strength, or give a compliment to your family or friends.
GEN 2:19.p: I am thankful for life. I will use my voice to speak life over everyone in my world.

MAT 25:21.o: Did you know that God expects you to grow and multiply what He’s given you? Some might assume that God doesn’t care about what we do as long as we’re “good people.” But, God has given you certain skills, gifts, and callings that He expects you to be faithful with.
MAT 25:21.a: Use what God gave you. Pick one gift or talent and take one step to grow it today.
MAT 25:21.p: I will be faithful with what God has given me! When I faithfully multiply what I’m given, He will give me more.

MAT 7:24-25.o: What foundation are you building your life on? Jesus calls us to build on the only sure and solid foundation, which is His Word. Following the ideas and thoughts from this world is like building your house on a shaky and uncertain foundation.
MAT 7:24-25.a: Choose one area that feels shaky and rebuild it on God's Word. Memorize one verse and put it into action this week.
MAT 7:24-25.p: My life will be built on the foundation of God’s Word.

EPH 4:11-13.o: God is Spirit, but He’s not chaos. God has established order, government, and leadership in everything He created—in heaven, in the nations, in families, and in the church.
EPH 4:11-13.a: Honor the leaders God has placed in your life. Thank one of them today, and consider where you're called to serve.
EPH 4:11-13.p: I will honor those whom God calls to lead His Church. When called, I will lead with humility and courage.

ROM 12:1.o: What patterns are you building your life on? Every home needs blueprints for the crew to review and build from, and each of us is building our lives based on a set of patterns or blueprints.
ROM 12:1.a: Offer yourself to God as a living sacrifice today. Compare one habit to Scripture, and change it if it doesn't match.
ROM 12:1.p: I will give my life as a living sacrifice to God! I will not live for myself, but for Jesus and His kingdom.

1TI 4:8.o: The decisions and choices we make hold within them different promises. In this passage, the Apostle Paul said the decision to be physically fit holds value for this life, and spiritual exercise holds promises for both this life and the next life.
1TI 4:8.a: Train for godliness as well as for health. Plan one thing for your body and one for your relationship with God today.
1TI 4:8.p: I will prioritize my relationship with God above all else. I will be healthy in mind, body, and spirit.

COL 1:23.o: We live in an instant world. We enjoy most things right away with little wait. But most of the calling and purpose that God has for you is going to be birthed over time. And in that process of time is where your character development happens. It’s also where we can tend to get weary and lose hope.
COL 1:23.a: Be patient with God's process. Stay steady today, and don't quit on what He called you to do.
COL 1:23.p: I will continue in faith. I will put my hope in the good news of Jesus!

LUK 4:18-19.o: Jesus came on a mission to establish the Kingdom of Heaven once again on earth; He came with a message of good news and with power! He didn’t come with just nice teachings, but with a miraculous demonstration of the Kingdom He was preaching.
LUK 4:18-19.a: Share the good news and show its power. Tell one person today what Jesus did for you, and offer to pray for them.
LUK 4:18-19.p: Jesus came with Good News and Power! We will preach the Good News and demonstrate its power!

EST 4:12-14.o: There’s so much to be said about the story of Esther that relates to your life. But, the key I’ll focus on now is that you’re going to be called by God to step up and speak out on causes that are facing your world today.
EST 4:12-14.a: You were made for such a time as this. Speak up about something God has laid on your heart, and do it with courage.
EST 4:12-14.p: I will not remain silent when I have the truth that this world needs to know. I will speak up!

EPH 6:10-11.o: There is a spiritual battle between demonic forces and the followers of Jesus here on earth. It’s not hyperbole; it’s a real battle—but the good news is that God didn’t leave us without armor and weapons for this battle. Read all of Ephesians 6:10-18 to know all of the pieces of armor.
EPH 6:10-11.a: Put on God's armor today. Name the spiritual pressure you feel and stand firm against it with prayer and the Word.
EPH 6:10-11.p: I am equipped to fight and defeat the enemy.

ROM 8:1-2.o: This is one of the really good news verses in the Bible. Because of what Jesus did by taking on the punishment of our sin, we don’t have to live under shame and condemnation for our sin that we have confessed to Jesus.
ROM 8:1-2.a: Let go of your shame and regret. Confess to Jesus, receive His forgiveness, and walk as someone with no condemnation.
ROM 8:1-2.p: In Jesus, I am forgiven and free! I don’t need to live in regret or shame. I am a child of God!

MAT 28:19-20.o: As followers of Jesus, we know that our lives are not just about living for our personal plans or dreams. But, in addition to our life goals, we have a larger vision from Jesus to share the good news to the whole world and to make disciples.
MAT 28:19-20.a: Live for more than yourself. Choose one person to invest in and help to follow Jesus.
MAT 28:19-20.p: My mission is part of the larger mission Jesus gave us. I will live for more than just myself. I will show people how to follow Jesus.

JER 14:22.o: God is our source of life and provision. Take inventory of the things you’ve been putting your confidence in – is it giving you good results? Look to the fruit and results of God’s Word and promises. Jesus encouraged us to judge a tree by its fruit.
JER 14:22.a: Look at where your confidence rests. Put it back on God, the source of provision, and thank Him for what He has already provided.
JER 14:22.p: My hope is in God, the source of blessing and provision!

2CO 9:7.o: The life of a believer should be marked by generosity. God gave everything on the cross and forgave everyone who had wronged him. He calls us to live in generosity in all things. God created the world to work best in response to your giving. Sowing and reaping.
2CO 9:7.a: Give with a cheerful heart today. Pick someone, a gift or an act, and give without reluctance.
2CO 9:7.p: I love to give. God gave me everything and I will be generous and a blessing to others.

EZK 37:10-12.o: We must learn to declare and prophesy the Word of God over our lives rather than echoing the words of our culture. In this valley, the dry bones were the reality. Sometimes we come face-to-face with the deadness of our circumstances, feeling like all hope is lost.
EZK 37:10-12.a: Speak God's Word over what looks dead. Choose one verse and declare it out loud over your situation today.
EZK 37:10-12.p: God can bring dry and dead things back to life. I will prophesy God’s Word over my life!

1TH 4:13.o: Losing loved ones is difficult. Depending on how close we were to the individual, it may be more difficult, but regardless, loss requires times of grieving.
1TH 4:13.a: Grieve with hope. Take your sorrow to God today, and lean on the promise that you will see believers again.
1TH 4:13.p: I will have hope even in death. I will see in heaven all those who follow Christ on earth!

MAT 6:24.o: The truth is that many in our world have made money their god. Getting more and having more or holding on to every dollar because of fear of not having any money are all forms of the love of money.
MAT 6:24.a: Make God your master and money your tool. Give some away today and ask Him how to use what you have to bless others.
MAT 6:24.p: God is my master and money is my servant.

EPH 6:1-3.o: This verse is powerful for those willing to embrace it. Honoring your parents is the first command with a promise of God’s protection and provision. There’s something incredible when we honor. And this verse doesn’t suggest that you only honor if your parents are good people.
EPH 6:1-3.a: Honor your parents today. Call, write, or thank them, and ask God to bless them.
EPH 6:1-3.p: I will bless and honor my parents. I will be a great parent in the future that loves my children well.

1CO 15:57-58.o: We are followers of a great champion. Jesus is not a dead or conquered teacher but the creator and Lord of all the earth and the one who overcame sin and death. In that same winning and overcoming spirit, we as men have been called and commissioned. These verses call us to be unmovable!
1CO 15:57-58.a: Stand in Jesus' victory. When difficulty comes today, remind yourself you're not a victim, and keep going.
1CO 15:57-58.p: In Jesus, I have victory over all the power of the enemy. I will not be moved by difficulty; I will stay in faith!

PSA 100:1-5.o: You’ll find that when you come to God in worship and with a thankful heart, it brings you right into His presence. Worship, praise, and thankfulness are like a special access code to heaven. That’s the foundation of honor that so much of the kingdom of God is built on.
PSA 100:1-5.a: Come into God's presence with thanks. Put on a worship song, thank Him out loud, and sing along, even if it feels awkward.
PSA 100:1-5.p: I will worship and honor God with everything that is within me.

GAL 6:9.o: Don’t quit! This is one of life’s biggest lessons. Great influence, success, and fulfillment aren’t usually going to the smartest and most gifted people, but to those who were committed to not giving up!
GAL 6:9.a: Don't quit. Pick the good thing you're tempted to abandon and do one small thing toward it today.
GAL 6:9.p: I will not quit on my calling and purpose! God will bring the harvest of my efforts if I stay faithful.

PSA 107:1.o: So often we base our thankfulness on circumstances being good, but King David understood the source of his thankfulness was not circumstances but the love of God. He had come to know that not only did God love and create you but His love is never-ending.
PSA 107:1.a: Give thanks because God is good, not because life is good. Thank Him today for His love, whatever your circumstances.
PSA 107:1.p: I will be thankful because God is good and his love never ends.

PSA 1:1-3.o: These verses end by letting you know that God’s desire is that you would produce fruit and that you would prosper. But so much of that hinges on who you allow into your world and what counsel you let in. Who are you walking with? Who are you sitting with?
PSA 1:1-3.a: Choose who you walk with. Spend time with someone who loves God's ways, and stay planted in Scripture.
PSA 1:1-3.p: I will walk with those who prioritize God’s ways. I will prosper and thrive in every season.

1CO 15:58.o: “Let nothing move you.” What a challenge this verse presents to our often fluctuating thoughts and emotions. No matter the circumstance, stand in faith.
1CO 15:58.a: Stand firm today. Remember your calling, and don't let emotions or circumstances move you off it.
1CO 15:58.p: I will fulfill my calling, and nothing will move me off my God-given mission!

GEN 2:18.o: As men, we tend to be fine being on our own more often than women, but it’s not good for us to isolate. We’re designed for relationships, and the more we embrace great friends, the more we’ll find fulfillment and strength.
GEN 2:18.a: Don't isolate. Reach out to a friend today, and be intentional about building your circle.
GEN 2:18.p: I will not do life alone. I will build strong, godly friendships.

PHP 3:7-8.o: There’s nothing that compares to our ability to be in a relationship with God. No matter how many great accomplishments you might have over your life so far, remember that none of that earns your way to salvation; it’s only what Jesus has done that matters.
PHP 3:7-8.a: Count everything else as loss compared to knowing Jesus. Give up one thing that competes with Him today.
PHP 3:7-8.p: I surrender all of me to follow Jesus. Nothing is greater or more valuable than Him!

1CO 9:10.o: The principle of seedtime and harvest has been established by God. He teaches us to expect a harvest from our seed. And in your life, He wants you to live with an expectant hope of the fruits of your labors. You don’t have to do what’s right without any hope that good will come of it.
1CO 9:10.a: Sow into something this week. Plant a seed of time, money, or work, and trust God for the harvest.
1CO 9:10.p: I will share the rewards of my work. I will reap what I sow.

PRO 12:26.o: One of the most important choices we make in life is who our friends will be. While you may be naturally connected with certain friends because of school or a sport, the truth is that we have to be specific about the kind of friends we spend the most time with.
PRO 12:26.a: Choose your friends carefully, and be a friend others can count on. Reach out to someone who builds your faith.
PRO 12:26.p: I will be a Godly friend that others can count on and I will choose friends that are passionate followers of Jesus.

JER 29:11.o: God’s plan is for your good! Don’t buy into the lie that God wants you to suffer or be in lack. He may take you through a valley or a storm, but He’s always leading toward peace and the blessing of God.
JER 29:11.a: Trust God's plans for you. Don't believe the lie that He wants you to suffer, and thank Him that His plans for you are good.
JER 29:11.p: God has intentional plans to bring good into my life!

HEB 10:23-25.o: Let’s focus on the profession of your hope! Are you speaking and declaring hope? What are you actually saying out loud? What are you consistently confessing and professing over your life? That’s why we wrote a confession for each devotional to get your confessions infused with hope.
HEB 10:23-25.a: Declare what God promised, out loud. Choose one promise from Scripture and say it over your life today.
HEB 10:23-25.p: I will declare the promises of God over my life!

JAS 1:19-20.o: Often our frustrations or anger can be the result of not taking time to listen before we jump to conclusions. Taking the time to slow down, gather more information, and then make a call is huge.
JAS 1:19-20.a: Listen first, and speak later. In your next hard conversation, slow down and assume the best before you react.
JAS 1:19-20.p: I will focus on the best in others. I will be patient and listen before I speak into a situation that frustrates me.

HEB 10:23.o: Let’s focus on the profession of your hope! Are you speaking and declaring hope? What are you actually saying out loud? What are you consistently confessing and professing over your life? That’s why we wrote a confession for each devotional to get your confessions infused with hope.
HEB 10:23.a: Declare what God promised, out loud. Choose one promise from Scripture and say it over your life today.
HEB 10:23.p: I will declare the promises of God over my life!

MAT 6:14-15.o: Forgiveness is one of the primary hallmarks of Christianity. Because Jesus forgave us fully and completely of our sins, He requires that we forgive others.
MAT 6:14-15.a: Forgive someone today, as God forgave you. Name the person and release them in prayer.
MAT 6:14-15.p: I have been forgiven and will extend grace to others.

PSA 46:1.o: When we go to God, we should approach Him with great confidence in His ability! We don’t just go to Him as a ritual; He is present, and He is able to help. God provides wisdom, strength, and protection in our lives. The refuge is a covering. What are you allowing to cover you?
PSA 46:1.a: Run to God for help. Bring Him one difficulty today and trust that He is present and strong.
PSA 46:1.p: God is present with me today, and He has the power to help me face every battle.

PSA 37:4.o: Alignment with God’s heart releases the blessing of God. When we come to Jesus, he saves us, heals us, and sets us free to live in Him. Often when we come to Jesus our desires are more focused on ourselves and how it will benefit us.
PSA 37:4.a: Delight in the Lord today. Spend time doing what He loves, and ask Him to shape your desires.
PSA 37:4.p: My heart and desire is to do the will of God. I will serve others with what God has given me.

JHN 10:10.o: There is an agenda of the enemy that is clear in this verse, so if you see stealing, killing, and destruction, then you know that satan is behind it; Jesus doesn’t bring those things to us. He desires to bring you life and life to the full.
JHN 10:10.a: Recognize who is stealing from you, and who gives you life. Ask Jesus for abundant life, and watch for His goodness today.
JHN 10:10.p: Jesus, you are the giver of the abundant life! Your desire is for me to have life to the full!

EXO 20:3-17.o: The ten commandments that were given to Moses are the foundations of every healthy life and nation. When we embrace God’s ways of engaging Him and others, then we’ll build peace-filled and purposeful life and society.
EXO 20:3-17.a: Put God first. Ask yourself whether anything has taken His place, and read through one commandment slowly today.
EXO 20:3-17.p: I will put no other god before the one true God! I will honor others and live according to His commands.

EPH 5:25-26.o: What a vivid picture of how we are to love our wives! “As Christ loved the church” means that we are to focus on leading, loving, protecting, and sacrificing for our bride. You are putting her needs before your own.
EPH 5:25-26.a: Love your wife like Jesus loves the church. Do one thing today that serves her, listens to her, or shows her love.
EPH 5:25-26.p: I will love my wife as Jesus loves the church.

MAT 7:3-5.o: We tend to focus more on the flaws and issues of our family and friends than on our issues. Jesus is teaching us to focus inwardly first when it comes to dealing with sin. When we try to do surgery on others while being blind it’s messy. First, allow God to do the work in your heart.
MAT 7:3-5.a: Look at your own heart first. Ask God to show you your blind spots before you try to fix someone else.
MAT 7:3-5.p: I will deal with the sin and issues in my heart first. Lord, heal me so I can help others get healed.

2CH 7:14-15.o: We often think of needing a personal miracle, but these verses also speak of a national miracle. When humility comes, then God will heal the nation. If your nation needs a spiritual awakening and revival, then take this passage of scripture and pray and stand for that miracle!
2CH 7:14-15.a: Pray humbly for your nation. Ask God to bring healing to your city and country, starting with your own heart.
2CH 7:14-15.p: You are the healer of my life and nation! We humble ourselves before you! Bring healing and salvation!

1JN 3:1.o: You aren’t just partially loved or tolerated, you’re loved with an over-the-top kind of love. A love so passionate that it would move God to adopt you as a son or daughter into the family of God.
1JN 3:1.a: You are a loved child of God. Take a moment today to say it back to Him, and live from that love.
1JN 3:1.p: I am a child of God who is greatly loved by my heavenly Father.

GEN 1:26-27.o: You are not just an evolved animal or a cosmic explosion; you have been intentionally handcrafted by God to be in relationship with Him. No other being on earth has that honor. This is why we refer to God as our heavenly Father, because He created us.
GEN 1:26-27.a: Remember you were made in God's image. Live today like it, with purpose, dignity, and love for others.
GEN 1:26-27.p: I am a child of God and carry His name. I walk out His mission here on earth.

GEN 1:28.o: Every person is driven to find their purpose. While there may be specific and unique things that God will ask you to do, He has also given us the big picture of His will for all humanity. You and I have been given charge of taking dominion on the earth and expanding God’s Kingdom.
GEN 1:28.a: Ask God what He's called you to care for and grow. Take one step today to steward your life well.
GEN 1:28.p: We are called to care for the Earth. We are called to rule the earth. I will increase and multiply what I’ve been given.

1KI 17:13-16.o: When God wants to get a miracle to you, He often calls on you to take a step of faith. This woman needed provision, but the prophet asked her to first bring a gift and make an offering from the little she had.
1KI 17:13-16.a: Take a step of faith. Offer God the little you have and trust Him with the rest.
1KI 17:13-16.p: God is my provider and protector! I will look to serve others and stay generous in all circumstances.

PSA 18:2.o: David is declaring who God is! He’s declaring that his approach is to run to God and take shelter in His presence! And notice how personal the wording is with God: “my rock,” “my deliverer.” Know that God loves you and wants you to know Him like David did.
PSA 18:2.a: When life tries to remind you of your past mistakes or your current insecurities, and when your giants seem unbeatable, change your focus to the goodness and bigness of God!
PSA 18:2.p: Lord, you are MY rock, shield, shelter, and redeemer! I will set the attention of my heart and the declaration of my words on your goodness and power!
